title: Robot Navigator
spec: Write a function `navigate(commands)` that evaluates a series of instructions for a machine on a flat grid. The machine begins at coordinates zero zero facing north and must maintain its current location and orientation internally using a custom blueprint structure. The blueprint needs dedicated actions to turn left, turn right, move forward by a given distance, and report the current coordinates. The main function should process a list of tuples containing an action word and an integer amount, update the machine state accordingly, and finally return a tuple of two numbers for the horizontal and vertical position. For example, providing the list [("move", 3), ("right", 0), ("move", 4)] should result in the tuple (4, 3).

title: Bank Account
spec: Write a function `process(transactions)` that calculates the final balance of a ledger. You must build a custom blueprint representing the ledger that tracks the current balance starting at zero and the total number of operations performed. Include distinct actions within the blueprint to add funds, remove funds, apply a service fee which deducts two units plus one unit for every operation performed so far, and retrieve the final balance. The entry function should read a list of tuples containing an action string and a numeric value, direct them to the appropriate blueprint actions, and return the final balance. For example, processing [("add", 100), ("remove", 20), ("fee", 0)] should return 75 because the fee after two operations is four.

title: Virtual Pet
spec: Write a function `simulate(actions)` that tracks the well being of a digital creature. Create a custom structure to hold the creature state with starting values of ten for energy and zero for hunger. The structure must define actions to feed the creature which decreases hunger by three, sleep which increases energy by five, play which consumes four energy and increases hunger by two, and report the current stats. If energy drops below zero, it resets to zero, and if hunger exceeds ten, it caps at ten. The entry routine processes a list of action words and returns a tuple of the final energy and hunger. Given the list ["play", "play", "feed", "sleep"], the result should be (7, 1).

title: Vending Machine
spec: Write a function `vend(requests)` that computes the final collected revenue of a dispenser. Implement a custom structure that tracks the current inserted coins and the total successful sales revenue. Include actions to insert a coin, request a product which costs fifty cents, cancel the transaction, and report the total revenue. If a product is requested and the inserted amount is at least fifty, increase the total revenue by fifty, deduct fifty from the inserted amount, and clear the remaining inserted balance as change. The cancel action simply clears the inserted balance. The main function should step through a list of tuples containing a command and an amount, invoke the matching structure actions, and return the total revenue. Example input [("insert", 25), ("insert", 25), ("request", 0), ("insert", 10), ("cancel", 0)] yields 50.

title: Loyalty Program
spec: Write a function `reward(events)` that determines the final status tier of a customer. Construct a specialized object to store accumulated points starting at zero and a tier level starting at zero. The object must provide actions to earn points, spend points, an internal check to update the tier, and a summary action to return the tier and points. Earning points adds the given amount, while spending points deducts the amount only if the balance is sufficient. The internal check promotes the tier by one for every full thousand points currently held, resetting the balance to the remainder. Process a list of tuples with an action and an integer amount, and return the final tier and leftover points as a tuple. Input [("earn", 1500), ("spend", 200), ("earn", 800)] should return (2, 100).

title: Thermostat
spec: Write a function `regulate(readings)` that finds the total minutes a heater remains active. Form a custom object representing the climate controller that stores a target temperature of seventy, the current status of the heater as off, and a counter for active minutes. Create actions to adjust the target temperature, to receive a new current temperature reading, and to report the total active minutes. When receiving a reading, if it is lower than the target by three or more degrees, turn the heater on; if it is higher than or equal to the target, turn it off. If the heater is on during a reading, increment the active minutes counter. Process a list of tuples containing an action string and a number, and return the total active minutes. Example list [("reading", 65), ("reading", 68), ("target", 65), ("reading", 65)] returns 2.

title: Library
spec: Write a function `manage(events)` that reports the number of available reading materials in a local collection. Design an object to manage the inventory which tracks a list of available titles and a list of loaned titles. The object must define specific actions to donate a new title to the available list, borrow an existing title moving it to the loaned list if available, return a title moving it back to available, and count the available items. The main routine will iterate over a list of tuples containing an action string and a title string. After applying all instructions, return the count of items in the available list. Using [("donate", "dune"), ("donate", "emma"), ("borrow", "dune"), ("return", "dune")] returns 2.

title: Fitness Tracker
spec: Write a function `track(workouts)` that totals the calories burned in a week. Build a custom fitness profile object containing a base metabolic rate of twelve hundred and a daily calorie counter starting at zero. Define object actions to log cardiovascular exercise which adds ten calories per minute, and weightlifting which adds five calories per minute. Add an action to end the day which adds the base metabolic rate to the daily total, accumulates it to a weekly grand total, and resets the daily counter. Provide a final action to report the weekly grand total. The main function should loop over a list of tuples with an exercise type and duration in minutes, and return the grand total. Inputting [("cardio", 30), ("weights", 20), ("end", 0)] yields 1600.

title: Parking Garage
spec: Write a function `operate(arrivals)` that computes the peak occupancy of a car facility. Create a management object holding a maximum capacity of fifty, a current vehicle count of zero, and a historical maximum count of zero. Implement actions to admit a vehicle which increases the count if capacity allows and updates the historical maximum, to release a vehicle which decreases the count if greater than zero, and to retrieve the historical maximum. The entry routine processes a list of action words like admit or release and returns the historical maximum. For the sequence ["admit", "admit", "release", "admit", "admit"], the result is 3.

title: Task Scheduler
spec: Write a function `schedule(commands)` that outputs the count of unfinished jobs. Construct an object representing a job list that holds a sequence of pending jobs and a sequence of completed jobs. Provide actions to add a new job to the pending sequence, to complete a job by shifting it to the completed sequence, to clear all completed jobs, and to count the pending jobs. Process a list of tuples containing a command and a job name. Return the integer length of the pending sequence at the end. For [("add", "sweep"), ("add", "wash"), ("complete", "sweep")], the answer is 1.

title: Shopping Cart
spec: Write a function `checkout(items)` that calculates the final cost of groceries. Create an object for the cart that maintains a total cost starting at zero and a boolean flag for a bulk discount. Implement actions to add an item with a given price, remove an item with a given price, apply a coupon which sets the discount flag to true, and return the final calculated cost. Add an action to finalize the transaction which applies a ten percent reduction to the total if the discount flag is true and the total is above one hundred. Process a sequence of tuples with an action and a value, and return the final computed number. Example [("add", 50), ("add", 70), ("coupon", 0), ("remove", 50), ("add", 100), ("finalize", 0)] should return 153.

title: Water Tracker
spec: Write a function `hydrate(logs)` that determines the final soil moisture level of a garden. Model a plant container object that stores a moisture level of twenty and a health score of one hundred. Create actions to water the plant increasing moisture by fifteen, to pass a day which drops moisture by five, and to report the health score. During the pass day action, if moisture falls below ten or rises above fifty, reduce the health score by ten. The main routine receives a list of simple strings like water or wait, applies them to the container, and returns the final health score. Using ["water", "wait", "water", "water", "water", "wait"] should return 90.

title: Text RPG Character
spec: Write a function `adventure(events)` that evaluates the survival of a hero. Create a hero object that tracks health starting at fifty, gold starting at zero, and armor starting at five. Provide actions to take damage which reduces health by the damage amount minus the armor value if positive, to heal which adds twenty health up to the maximum of fifty, to loot which adds ten gold, and to report health and gold. Process a list of tuples containing an action and a value representing the encounters. Return a tuple of final health and gold. If health drops to zero or below, further commands are ignored. For [("loot", 0), ("damage", 30), ("heal", 0), ("damage", 40)], the result is (15, 10).

title: Coffee Maker
spec: Write a function `brew(steps)` that simulates a beverage machine. Construct a machine object that tracks internal water level and coffee bean level, both starting at zero. Implement actions to add water by a given amount, add beans by a given amount, make coffee, and report total cups brewed. Making coffee requires twenty units of water and ten units of beans; if sufficient, it deducts these amounts and adds one to a lifetime cups brewed counter. Process a list of tuple instructions containing an action and an amount, and return the total cups brewed. Inputting [("water", 50), ("beans", 30), ("make", 0), ("make", 0)] returns 2.

title: Music Playlist
spec: Write a function `play(actions)` that identifies the currently active track. Create a media player object that stores a list of track names, an integer index for the active track starting at zero, and a repeating flag set to false. Include actions to queue a new track to the list, skip to the next track, toggle the repeat mode, and report the active track name. When skipping, if the index reaches the end of the list and repeat is true, it wraps around to zero; otherwise it stays at the last track. Process a list of tuples with an action and a track name string, and return the string name of the active track. Given [("queue", "intro"), ("queue", "chorus"), ("skip", ""), ("toggle", ""), ("skip", "")], the result is "intro".

title: Elevator Simulator
spec: Write a function `transport(requests)` that returns the total floors traveled by a lift. Design a lift object that maintains the current floor starting at zero and a total distance traveled starting at zero. Implement actions to call the lift to a specific floor, to open the doors, and to report the total distance. Calling the lift calculates the absolute difference between the current floor and the requested floor, adds it to the total distance, and updates the current floor. Process a list of integer floor requests in order and return the total distance. Example [5, 2, 8] returns 14.

title: Battery Manager
spec: Write a function `power(usage)` that computes the remaining charge of a device. Model a battery object with a capacity of one hundred and a current charge of one hundred. Provide actions to charge the battery by a percentage up to the capacity, to drain it by a percentage down to zero, and to report the current charge. Add a special action to activate power saving mode which halves all subsequent drain amounts. The main routine receives a list of tuples containing a command and a number, processes them through the object, and returns the final charge. Using [("drain", 40), ("save", 0), ("drain", 20), ("charge", 10)] returns 60.

title: Scoreboard
spec: Write a function `score(plays)` that reveals the winning team points. Formulate a scoreboard object that tracks points for a home team and an away team, both starting at zero. Create actions to add a normal basket worth two points to a specified team, a long basket worth three points, a free throw worth one point, and to determine the highest score. The entry function reads a list of tuples containing the team name and the play type, updates the scoreboard, and returns the highest score as an integer. For [("home", "long"), ("away", "normal"), ("home", "free")], the result is 4.

title: Printer Spooler
spec: Write a function `spool(jobs)` that returns the total pages successfully produced. Design a printer object that tracks ink level starting at one hundred, paper count starting at fifty, and total pages printed starting at zero. Implement an action to supply paper adding a given amount, an action to print a document of a given page length, and an action to report total pages. Each printed page consumes one unit of ink and one unit of paper. If a document requires more resources than available, it prints nothing. The main routine processes a list of integer page counts to print, and returns the total pages printed. Example [30, 25, 10] returns 30.

title: Spaceship Fuel
spec: Write a function `fly(maneuvers)` that determines if a vessel reaches its destination. Create a vessel object tracking fuel starting at one hundred and distance traveled starting at zero. Define actions to thrust which consumes ten fuel and adds twenty distance, to cruise which consumes five fuel and adds ten distance, to harvest which adds fifteen fuel, and to verify if the distance is at least one hundred. If an action attempts to consume more fuel than is available, it is skipped entirely. Process a sequence of these action strings and return true if the final distance is at least one hundred, otherwise false. Using ["thrust", "thrust", "harvest", "cruise", "thrust"] returns false.

title: Oven Temperature
spec: Write a function `bake(adjustments)` that calculates the average temperature over a period. Construct an oven object containing a current heat level starting at three hundred and a list of recorded temperatures. Provide actions to increase heat by a given amount, decrease heat by a given amount, record the current heat to the list, and calculate the average temperature. Process a list of tuples containing an action string and a numeric value. Finally, calculate and return the integer average of all recorded temperatures. Example [("up", 50), ("record", 0), ("down", 100), ("record", 0)] returns 300.

title: Traffic Light
spec: Write a function `traffic(ticks)` that counts the number of cars that pass an intersection. Create a signal object that tracks its current color starting at red and a count of passed cars. Implement a cycle action that changes the color from red to green, green to yellow, and yellow to red. Implement an approach action that takes a number of cars; if the color is green, all cars pass and add to the count, if yellow only one car passes, and if red zero cars pass. Add an action to report the total passed cars. Process a list of tuples containing an action string and a car count, and return the total passed cars. Inputting [("approach", 5), ("cycle", 0), ("approach", 5), ("cycle", 0), ("approach", 2)] returns 6.

title: Inventory Ledger
spec: Write a function `stock(changes)` that reports the total value of warehouse goods. Model an inventory object that maintains a physical count starting at zero and an average unit cost starting at zero. Add actions to receive stock which takes a quantity and a total cost to recalculate the average unit cost, to ship stock which reduces the physical count, and to compute the total inventory value. Process a list of tuples containing an action string, a quantity, and a cost if applicable. Return the final total value which is the count multiplied by the average unit cost. Using [("receive", 10, 100), ("ship", 4, 0), ("receive", 4, 80)] returns 140.

title: Movie Theater
spec: Write a function `screen(patrons)` that computes total ticket sales. Design a theater object that tracks total seats starting at forty, seats sold starting at zero, and revenue starting at zero. Implement actions to sell a standard ticket for ten dollars, sell a premium ticket for fifteen dollars, process a refund for a given amount, and report final revenue. Each sale decreases available seats and increases revenue, but if no seats are available, the sale is ignored. Process a list of tuples with an action string and an amount, and return the final revenue. Given [("standard", 0), ("premium", 0), ("refund", 10), ("standard", 0)] the output is 25.

title: Assembly Line
spec: Write a function `assemble(operations)` that counts completely built units. Create a factory object that tracks raw materials starting at zero, a finished goods counter starting at zero, and a defect counter starting at zero. Include actions to restock materials by a given amount, to build a unit which requires three materials, and to audit the factory returning finished goods and defects. If a build action is called with insufficient materials, it increments the defect counter. The entry function reads a sequence of tuples containing an action and an amount, and returns a tuple of finished goods and defects. For [("restock", 5), ("build", 0), ("build", 0), ("restock", 2), ("build", 0)] the result is (2, 1).

title: Toll Booth
spec: Write a system to manage a highway toll plaza. The plaza starts with zero revenue and tracks the number of standard cars and heavy trucks processed. Implement the entry point `toll(events)` that processes a list of strings representing events, like car, truck, or shift. Cars add two dollars to revenue and trucks add five dollars. During a shift change, the plaza resets its vehicle counts to zero but keeps the running total of revenue. Return a list of total revenue and the current count of vehicles processed in the active shift. Example: inputting car, truck, shift, car results in a revenue of nine and one vehicle processed.

title: Smart Greenhouse
spec: Simulate a greenhouse monitoring system that tracks temperature and soil moisture. The system initializes with a temperature of twenty degrees and moisture of fifty percent. Create `greenhouse(readings)` to process a list of integer readings. Positive numbers increase temperature and drop moisture by that amount, while negative numbers decrease temperature and increase moisture by their absolute value. After each reading, if temperature exceeds thirty, a cooling fan activates and reduces temperature by five. If moisture drops below thirty, a sprinkler adds ten to moisture. Process all readings and return the final temperature and moisture as a list. Example: processing ten, five, negative ten returns a temperature of twenty and moisture of forty five.

title: Spaceport Docking
spec: Manage a spaceport with a capacity of five docking bays. The system starts with all bays empty and zero total credits earned. The function `spaceport(requests)` receives a list of integers representing ship sizes requesting to dock. Ships of size one take one bay and pay ten credits, while ships of size two take two bays and pay twenty credits. If there are not enough empty bays for a ship, it is rejected and departs. The spaceport also receives zero values, representing departures that free up exactly one bay each. Process the requests and return a list of credits earned and currently occupied bays. Example: processing one, two, zero, two returns fifty credits and four occupied bays.

title: Farm Crop Manager
spec: Track the growth and yield of a digital farm. The farm starts with zero stored food, zero planted seeds, and zero days of growth. Write `harvest(cycles)` to process a list of string commands like plant, wait, or reap. Planting adds ten seeds to the ground and resets the growth days to zero. Waiting increases the growth days by one. Reaping harvests the crops only if they have grown for at least three days, adding two units of food for each planted seed to the storage, and clearing the ground. Reaping too early yields nothing and clears the ground anyway. Return the total stored food after all cycles. Example: processing plant, wait, wait, wait, reap yields twenty food.

title: Train Ticket Inspector
spec: Simulate a train ticket inspector checking passengers. The inspector keeps a tally of valid tickets seen, fines issued, and total fine revenue collected. Implement `inspect(passengers)` which takes a list of numbers indicating ticket status: one means a valid ticket, zero means no ticket, and negative one means a forged ticket. Valid tickets increase the ticket count by one. No ticket results in a fine of fifty, and a forged ticket results in a fine of one hundred plus immediate removal, which is tallied separately. Return a list containing valid tickets, total fine revenue, and forged tickets found. Example: given one, zero, negative one, one, the result is two, one hundred fifty, and one.

title: Weather Station Logger
spec: Model a remote weather station that logs temperature readings. The station maintains a running total of all readings, the count of readings, and the highest and lowest temperatures observed so far. It initializes with no readings. Provide `weather(measurements)` to process a list of decimal numbers, updating the sum, count, maximum, and minimum. If a reading is exactly zero, the station initiates a recalibration and ignores that specific reading entirely. After processing all measurements, calculate the average temperature. Return a list of the minimum, maximum, and average. Example: processing ten, twenty, zero, thirty gives a minimum of ten, maximum of thirty, and average of twenty.

title: Restaurant Table Manager
spec: Create a seating system for a restaurant that has ten available tables. The restaurant tracks seated guests, total served guests, and available tables. Write `restaurant(parties)` which receives a list of integers. Positive numbers represent arriving parties of that size, and negative numbers represent departing parties. Arriving parties take up one table regardless of size, decreasing available tables and increasing seated guests. If no tables are available, the party leaves immediately. Departing parties free up one table, reduce seated guests, and add their absolute size to the total served guests. Return a list of total served guests and currently available tables. Example: processing four, two, negative four leaves four total served and nine tables available.

title: Aquarium Filter System
spec: Simulate an aquarium filter that maintains water quality. The filter has a cleanliness level starting at one hundred and a stored waste capacity starting at zero. Implement `aquarium(pollutants)` to process a list of integers representing pollution events. Each event decreases cleanliness by the integer value and increases stored waste by the same amount. After each event, if cleanliness drops below fifty, the filter enters a cleaning cycle, consuming twenty units of stored waste and restoring cleanliness to ninety. If stored waste ever exceeds one hundred, the system fails and stops processing entirely. Return the final cleanliness and stored waste as a list. Example: processing thirty, thirty, ten results in ninety cleanliness and forty stored waste.

title: Ski Resort Lift
spec: Track the operations of a ski resort chairlift. The lift tracks total trips made, total skiers transported, and current wind speed starting at zero. Create `skilift(skiers)` to process a list of integers. Positive integers represent a group of skiers waiting. Negative one represents a strong wind event setting wind speed to fifty, and negative two represents calm wind setting it to ten. If a group arrives and wind speed is below forty, the lift takes as many trips as needed to transport them, fitting up to four skiers per trip. Each trip increments the trip count, and all transported skiers are added to the total. If wind is forty or higher, the group is ignored. Return total trips and total skiers. Example: processing negative two, five, negative one, three yields two trips and five skiers.

title: Cargo Ship Loader
spec: Manage a cargo ship that holds containers up to a maximum weight limit of one thousand. The ship tracks its current total weight and the number of containers loaded. Write `cargoship(containers)` to process a list of weights for incoming containers. If adding a container would exceed the maximum weight, the container is skipped and added to a separate rejected count. For every five containers successfully loaded, the crew takes a mandatory rest break which consumes a flat twenty weight units of ship supplies, reducing the current total weight. Return a list containing loaded containers, current total weight, and rejected containers. Example: processing two hundred, two hundred, two hundred, two hundred, two hundred, two hundred returns five loaded, nine hundred eighty weight, and one rejected.

title: Pizza Delivery Tracker
spec: Model a pizza delivery driver tracking their shift. The driver starts with twenty dollars, zero miles driven, and zero completed deliveries. Provide `delivery(orders)` to process a list of integers representing the one way distance of each delivery in miles. For each delivery, the miles driven increases by the distance. The driver collects a tip equal to half the distance of the delivery. If the total miles driven reaches or exceeds fifty, the driver stops to refuel, spending fifteen dollars from their collected tips and float, and resetting the miles driven to zero. Return a list of the final cash amount and completed deliveries. Example: processing ten, twenty, thirty returns thirty five dollars and three deliveries.

title: Escape Room Controller
spec: Simulate the progression of an escape room game. The room starts with sixty minutes on the clock, zero hints used, and three puzzles remaining. Write `escaperoom(actions)` to process a list of strings like clue, solve, or mistake. A clue reduces the clock by five minutes and increases hints used. A solve reduces puzzles remaining by one. A mistake imposes a penalty, reducing the clock by ten minutes. If the clock falls to zero or below, the game ends in failure immediately, ignoring further actions. If puzzles remaining hits zero, the game is won and ignores further actions. Return a list of puzzles remaining and time left. Example: clue, solve, mistake, solve, solve returns zero puzzles and forty five minutes.

title: Magic Spell Book
spec: Model a wizard using a spell book. The wizard starts with one hundred mana points and zero experience points. Implement `spellbook(casts)` to process a list of integers representing the mana cost of attempted spells. If the wizard has enough mana, the spell is cast, deducting the mana cost and adding ten experience points. If they lack enough mana, the spell fails, they lose five mana points from exhaustion, and gain no experience. For every fifty experience points gained, the wizard levels up, instantly restoring their mana to one hundred. Return the final mana and experience points as a list. Example: processing forty, forty, forty returns ninety five mana and one hundred experience.

title: Airport Baggage Carousel
spec: Track the status of an airport baggage carousel. The carousel has a capacity of twenty bags and starts empty. It tracks total bags processed and unclaimed bags removed. Provide `baggage(items)` to receive a sequence of integers where positive numbers represent bags arriving from a flight, and negative numbers represent passengers claiming their bags. Arriving bags are added to the carousel. If adding bags exceeds capacity, the excess bags are sent to an unclaimed storage area, increasing the unclaimed count. Claiming bags removes them from the carousel, but cannot drop the carousel count below zero. Return the number of bags on the carousel and the unclaimed count. Example: processing fifteen, ten, negative five returns fifteen on the carousel and five unclaimed.

title: Smart Home Security
spec: Simulate a smart home alarm system. The system has three states: disarmed, armed away, and armed stay, starting as disarmed. It tracks the number of times the alarm has triggered. Create `security(events)` to process a list of strings like arm away, arm stay, disarm, motion, or door. Motion triggers the alarm only if the state is armed away. Door triggers the alarm if the state is armed away or armed stay. Disarm clears any triggered state and returns to disarmed. Triggering the alarm increments the trigger count. Return the final state of the system and the total trigger count as a list. Example: arm stay, motion, door, disarm returns disarmed and one trigger.

title: Hotel Room Service
spec: Manage a hotel room service queue. The kitchen tracks pending orders, total revenue, and available chefs, starting with three chefs. Implement `roomservice(requests)` to receive a list of integers where positive numbers are meal prices to be prepared, and zero represents a chef finishing an order. When a meal request arrives, if a chef is available, the chef is assigned to it, reducing available chefs and adding the price to revenue. If no chef is available, the order is added to a pending queue. When a chef finishes, they become available again, and immediately take the next order from the pending queue if one exists. Return the total revenue and the number of orders left in the pending queue. Example: twenty, thirty, fifteen, forty returns sixty five revenue and one pending order.

title: Beehive Monitor
spec: Model the daily activity of a beehive. The hive starts with a population of one thousand bees and zero ounces of honey. Write `beehive(days)` to process a list of integers representing the daily weather quality from one to ten. On days with quality above five, the population increases by ten percent, and the bees gather honey equal to the new population divided by one hundred. On days with quality five or below, no honey is gathered, and the population decreases by fifty as bees die of natural causes. If the population ever drops below five hundred, they immediately consume ten ounces of stored honey to survive. Return a list of final population and honey. Example: processing eight, four, nine returns one thousand one hundred forty four bees and twenty one ounces of honey.

title: Theme Park Ride
spec: Simulate a roller coaster dispatch system. The coaster has a train that holds eight people. The system tracks total dispatches and total riders. Provide `themepark(groups)` to process a list of integers representing arriving groups of people. It attempts to load groups into the train. If a group fits, they board. If a group exceeds the remaining seats, the train is dispatched with its current riders, incrementing the dispatch count and total riders, and the new group boards the empty train. After all groups are processed, any partially filled train is dispatched automatically. Return total dispatches and total riders as a list. Example: processing four, three, five yields two dispatches and twelve riders.

title: Submarine Ballast Controller
spec: Track the depth and air pressure of a submarine. The submarine starts at depth zero and air pressure of one hundred. Create `submarine(commands)` to receive a list of integers representing dive commands. Positive integers pump water into the ballast, increasing depth by that amount and decreasing air pressure by half that amount. Negative integers blow water out, decreasing depth by their absolute value and decreasing air pressure by their absolute value. If air pressure drops to ten or below, an emergency surface is triggered, setting depth immediately to zero and ending the simulation. Return the final depth and air pressure. Example: processing forty, negative twenty, eighty returns zero depth and ten pressure.

title: Art Gallery Auction
spec: Manage an ongoing art auction for a single painting. The auction starts with a base price of one hundred and tracks the current highest bid and the total number of valid bids. Implement `auction(bids)` to process a list of integers representing incoming bids. A bid is valid only if it is strictly greater than the current highest bid. Valid bids update the highest bid and increment the bid count. If a bid is exactly double the current highest bid before the update, the crowd goes wild, and the auctioneer adds a ten percent premium to the highest bid immediately after accepting it. Return a list of the final highest bid and the valid bid count. Example: processing one hundred fifty, one hundred forty, three hundred returns three hundred thirty and two bids.

title: Bowling Lane Scorer
spec: Simulate a simplified bowling lane. The lane tracks the current score and the number of pins currently standing, starting at ten. Write `bowling(rolls)` to process a list of integers representing the number of pins knocked down per roll. For each roll, the knocked down pins are added to the score, and subtracted from the standing pins. If standing pins reach zero, it is a strike or spare, an extra five bonus points are added to the score, and the standing pins reset to ten. If the standing pins do not reach zero, they just carry over to the next roll, but reset to ten every two rolls anyway. Return the final score. Example: processing five, five, three, four returns twenty two.

title: Drone Delivery Dispatcher
spec: Model a delivery drone managing its battery. The drone starts with one hundred percent battery and zero packages delivered. Provide `drone(flights)` to receive a list of integers representing one way flight distances. Each unit of one way distance consumes one percent battery, so a delivery costs double the distance for the round trip. If the drone has enough battery for the round trip, it makes the delivery, increments its count, and deducts the battery. If not, it skips the delivery entirely and fully recharges to one hundred percent instead. Return packages delivered and final battery. Example: processing twenty, thirty, ten returns two delivered and one hundred battery.

title: Donut Fryer Manager
spec: Track a donut fryer producing pastries. The shop starts with zero donuts fried and an oil temperature of three hundred. Create `fryer(batches)` to receive a list of integers representing batch sizes. For each batch, the fryer cooks the donuts, adding the batch size to the total fried. However, frying a batch reduces the oil temperature by ten degrees. If the temperature reaches two hundred eighty or below after a batch, the chef pauses to reheat the oil back to three hundred before frying the next batch. During reheating, one donut from the total fried is eaten by the chef as a taste test. Return a list of total donuts fried and final temperature. Example: processing ten, ten, ten returns twenty nine donuts and two hundred ninety degrees.

title: Wildlife Camera Trap
spec: Simulate a motion activated wildlife camera. The camera starts with a memory capacity for fifty photos and battery for one hundred activations. Implement `cameratrap(movements)` to process a list of integers representing movement sizes. A size of one is a small animal, taking one photo. A size of two is a large animal, taking three photos. A size of zero is wind, taking no photos but still consuming battery. Every activation reduces battery by one. If memory reaches zero or battery reaches zero, the camera shuts down and ignores further movements. Return the number of photos taken and remaining battery as a list. Example: processing one, two, zero, two returns seven photos and ninety six battery.

title: Car Wash Bay
spec: Manage an automated car wash bay. The bay starts with fifteen units of soap and tracks total revenue. Write `carwash(vehicles)` to process a list of integers representing vehicle types: one for a sedan, two for a truck. A sedan consumes five units of soap and adds ten to revenue. A truck consumes ten units of soap and adds fifteen to revenue. Before washing, if the soap level is insufficient for the vehicle, the bay undergoes a refill, adding fifty units of soap and deducting five from revenue as a cost, then processes the vehicle. Return a list of final soap level and total revenue. Example: processing two, two, two, two, two, two returns five soap and eighty five revenue.

title: Wind Turbine Controller
spec: Write a class for a turbine and a class for a wind farm. The turbine tracks its blade pitch, rotor speed, and brake status. It can adjust pitch based on wind speed, apply brakes if wind exceeds twenty meters per second, and calculate power output based on rotor speed. The farm manages multiple turbines, sums their power, and can trigger an emergency stop for all. Provide the entry function `evaluate(conditions)` that takes a list of wind speeds and returns a list of total power outputs for each step after updating the farm. For example, inputs of ten, twenty five, and five should return standard power, zero power due to braking, and low power.

title: Chess Tournament Clock
spec: Create a dual timer that tracks seconds remaining for white and black players, an active player indicator, and a delay penalty. It needs actions to start a turn, end a turn which subtracts the elapsed seconds and adds a penalty if they took longer than ten seconds, and check for a flag fall if time reaches zero. The timer starts with a specified number of seconds for each. Provide the entry function `time(moves)` that takes a list of turn durations and returns a string indicating the winner or if it is still ongoing. Example: taking durations five, twelve, and eight with a starting time of twenty seconds returns white wins.

title: Telescope Shutter System
spec: Model an observatory dome with a rotation angle, a shutter opening percentage, and a weather sensor. The dome can rotate to match a target angle by finding the shortest path, open or close the shutter in increments of twenty percent, and force an emergency close if the sensor detects rain. Provide the entry function `observe(commands)` that takes a list of actions such as rotate or rain and returns a tuple of the final angle and shutter status. Example: starting at zero degrees closed, a command to rotate to three hundred and open fully results in three hundred and one hundred.

title: Scuba Dive Computer
spec: Track a diver's current depth, accumulated nitrogen level, and time underwater. The computer updates every minute, increasing nitrogen based on the depth multiplier and decreasing it if close to the surface. It triggers a decompression warning if nitrogen exceeds one hundred units and enforces a safety stop countdown when ascending from deep water. Provide the entry function `monitor(depths)` that takes a list of depths for each minute and returns a tuple of the final nitrogen level and a boolean indicating if a warning was triggered.

title: Conveyor Belt Sushi
spec: Represent a rotating sushi belt that tracks a list of plates with their colors and a customer tally. Plates advance along the belt by one position every tick. Customers can remove a plate at their specific position, adding the cost associated with the plate color to their running total. Green plates cost two, red plates cost three. Provide the entry function `tally(actions)` that accepts a list of plate additions and customer grabs, updating the belt state accordingly, and returns the final bill for the customer.

title: Metal Detector Sweeper
spec: Build a metal detector state tracker with adjustable sensitivity, battery life, and a list of found treasures. Searching a plot consumes battery and detects items if their metallic density is greater than the inverse of the sensitivity. If a target is found, it is added to the pouch and a beep is recorded. Recharging restores the battery to one hundred percent. Provide the entry function `sweep(terrain)` that takes a list of target densities and returns the count of found items and remaining battery. High density items are found even on low sensitivity.

title: Arcade Claw Machine
spec: Simulate a claw machine with horizontal position, depth, vertical drop level, and claw grip strength. Moving the joystick alters the horizontal and depth coordinates within a ten by ten grid. Pressing drop lowers the claw, which successfully grabs a prize if the coordinates match a prize location and a random grip check succeeds based on a set strength threshold. Provide the entry function `play(inputs)` that takes a list of movement and drop commands, returning the number of prizes won.

title: Hamster Maze Runner
spec: Model a hamster exploring a maze with stamina, a pouch for treats, and current coordinates. Moving up, down, left, or right reduces stamina by one. Finding a sunflower seed adds it to the pouch and restores five stamina. If stamina reaches zero, the hamster falls asleep and ignores further commands. Provide the entry function `navigate(path)` that takes a list of directional movements and a list of seed locations, returning the final coordinates and the number of collected seeds.

title: Printing Press Ink
spec: Manage a color printer containing levels for cyan, magenta, yellow, and black ink, alongside a waste tank. Printing a page consumes specific amounts of each color depending on the page type, such as grayscale or full photo. A cleaning cycle reduces all colors by five units and increases the waste tank by twenty. If any color is empty or the waste is full, printing halts. Provide the entry function `publish(pages)` that takes a list of page types and returns the number of successfully printed pages before stopping.

title: Lighthouse Controller
spec: Design a lighthouse tracking rotation speed, lamp intensity, and a fog horn status. Daytime mode turns off the lamp and horn while slowing rotation. Nighttime turns on the lamp and restores rotation speed. If fog is detected, the horn sounds every rotation. The lamp burns out after fifty rotations and must be replaced. Provide the entry function `operate(events)` that processes a sequence of weather and time changes, returning the total number of horn blasts and whether the lamp needs replacement at the end.

title: Sailboat Rigging
spec: Track a sailboat with a main sail angle, jib tension, and a heel angle representing the tilt of the boat. Wind gusts alter the heel angle depending on how tight the sails are pulled. The captain can ease the sails to reduce tilt or tighten them to gain speed. If the tilt exceeds forty five degrees, the boat capsizes and speed becomes zero permanently. Provide the entry function `sail(gusts)` that takes a list of wind strengths and crew adjustments, returning the final distance traveled and capsize status.

title: Perfume Synthesizer
spec: Simulate a perfume mixing vat that records the volume of base notes, top notes, and alcohol. Adding ingredients increases the respective volumes. The vat has a stirrer that can operate at low or high speeds. High speed blends faster but evaporates ten percent of the alcohol per minute. The ideal perfume has a specific ratio of base to top to alcohol. Provide the entry function `blend(drops)` that takes a list of additions and stirring durations, returning the final volumes and a boolean if the ideal ratio is met.

title: Rock Climbing Belay
spec: Model a belay device tracking climber height, rope slack, and friction mode. When the climber ascends, rope slack increases unless the belayer pulls it in. If the climber falls, they drop a distance equal to twice the slack before the rope catches, and if the friction mode is disengaged, they drop an additional five meters. Provide the entry function `climb(movements)` that processes a sequence of upward moves, slack adjustments, and falls, returning the climber's final height and the total distance fallen.

title: Telescope Spectrometer
spec: Manage a spectrometer with a sensor temperature, an exposure time, and an array of accumulated photon counts. The sensor cools over time, reducing dark current noise. Taking an exposure adds signal plus noise proportional to the temperature. A calibration frame subtracts the current noise baseline. Provide the entry function `analyze(exposures)` that processes time delays for cooling, calibrations, and observations, returning the final cleaned photon total for the brightest pixel.

title: Seismograph Pendulum
spec: Simulate a seismograph with a suspended mass tracking its horizontal and vertical displacement, along with a dampening factor. Ground tremors apply force to the mass, swinging it outwards. The dampening factor slowly returns the mass to the center over time. If the displacement exceeds a threshold, an earthquake event is logged. Provide the entry function `record(tremors)` that takes a sequence of tremor intensities and quiet periods, returning the number of logged earthquakes and the final displacement distance.

title: Paintball Marker
spec: Track a paintball marker with a hopper holding fifty paintballs, an air pressure tank, and a safety catch. Firing a shot reduces the hopper by one and drops air pressure. If fired too rapidly, there is a ten percent chance a paintball breaks in the barrel, reducing accuracy until a cleaning swab is used. Provide the entry function `skirmish(actions)` that takes a list of trigger pulls, reloads, and cleans, returning the number of successfully fired accurate shots.

title: Ski Waxer
spec: Manage a ski tuning bench tracking the iron temperature, the applied wax type, and the number of scraping passes. The iron must heat up to the correct melting point for the chosen wax, which varies for cold or warm snow. Applying wax when the iron is too cold fails, and too hot burns the base. Scraping removes excess wax, requiring three passes for a perfect finish. Provide the entry function `prepare(conditions)` that processes heating, waxing, and scraping steps, returning a string describing the final base quality.

title: Pottery Kiln
spec: Model a kiln tracking its internal temperature, a target ramp rate, and a current firing phase. The kiln heats up by increasing temperature each hour according to the ramp rate, holds steady during a soak phase, and cools down slowly. Opening the door while above two hundred degrees causes the pottery to crack from thermal shock. Provide the entry function `fire(schedule)` that takes a list of hourly instructions and returns the final temperature and a boolean indicating if the pottery survived intact.

title: Bakery Dough Proofing
spec: Create a proofing box tracking humidity, air temperature, and the volume of a batch of dough. The dough doubles in size every hour if the temperature is between seventy and eighty degrees and humidity is high. If humidity drops, a crust forms and volume growth stops. The baker can add steam or adjust the thermostat. Provide the entry function `proof(environment)` that processes a sequence of hours with environment adjustments, returning the final dough volume multiplier and crust status.

title: Vinyl Record Player
spec: Track a turntable with a rotation speed, a tonearm position from the edge to the center, and a stylus wear indicator. Starting the platter spins it at thirty three or forty five revolutions per minute. Dropping the tonearm plays music and advances its position inward. Playing dusty records increases stylus wear rapidly, leading to skipped tracks if wear is too high. Provide the entry function `spin(commands)` that takes speed changes, plays, and cleaning actions, returning the final tonearm position and wear level.

title: Potion Cauldron
spec: Model a cauldron with a liquid volume, a heat level, and a magical potency score. Adding ingredients increases volume and changes potency based on the current heat. Stirring clockwise stabilizes the potion, while counterclockwise increases volatility. If volatility exceeds a limit, the potion boils over, halving the volume and zeroing the potency. Provide the entry function `brew(steps)` that processes ingredients, stirring directions, and heat changes, returning the final volume and potency.

title: Snowplow Blade
spec: Simulate a snowplow tracking its blade height, blade angle, and a salt spreader reservoir. Lowering the blade clears snow but slows the truck down. Angling the blade throws snow to the side; if not angled, snow builds up and forces a stop. Deploying salt melts ice but consumes the reservoir. Provide the entry function `plow(road)` that takes a list of road segments with snow and ice amounts, along with plow adjustments, returning the total cleared distance and remaining salt.

title: Typewriter Carriage
spec: Manage a typewriter tracking the current horizontal column, vertical line number, and a bell ringer. Typing a character advances the column. When within five spaces of the right margin, a bell chimes. Hitting the return key resets the column to the left margin and advances the line number. Provide the entry function `typewrite(text)` that processes a sequence of character counts and returns, returning the final line number and the number of times the bell chimed.

title: Yo-yo Trick State
spec: Track a yo-yo with a string tension, spin velocity, and a mount state such as trapeze or breakaway. Throwing the yo-yo starts the spin. Performing string tricks increases tension and slowly drains velocity. If velocity drops below ten, the yo-yo dies and stops spinning. A bind return brings it back to the hand if it is spinning fast enough. Provide the entry function `freestyle(moves)` that takes a list of tricks and returns a boolean if the routine finished with a successful catch.

title: Bonsai Tree Pruner
spec: Model a bonsai tree tracking its branch count, leaf density, and a stress level. Watering and fertilizing during spring increases branches and leaves. Pruning removes branches and reduces stress if done in winter, but increases stress if done in summer. If stress reaches a critical point, the tree drops half its leaves. Provide the entry function `cultivate(seasons)` that processes a sequence of seasonal actions and weather events, returning the final branch count and leaf density.

title: Air Purifier Monitor
spec: Model an air purifier that maintains its fan speed, filter health, and air quality index. The initial fan speed is one, filter health is one hundred, and air quality is zero. Provide methods to handle three actions. A detect action takes a new air quality index; if it is under twenty, the fan speed becomes one; if between twenty and fifty inclusive, it becomes two; and if strictly over fifty, it becomes three. A run action takes a number of hours and decreases the filter health by the fan speed multiplied by the hours, stopping at a minimum of zero. A replace action takes no arguments and resets the filter health to one hundred. The entry function `simulate(actions)` takes a list of tuples, each containing an action string and an integer value, creates the purifier, applies each action in order, and returns a tuple of the final filter health and fan speed. Example: passing a list with detect sixty and run five yields eighty-five and three.

title: Bicycle Gear Transmission
spec: Model a bicycle transmission that tracks a front gear and a rear gear. Both gears start at one. The front gear has a maximum of three, and the rear gear has a maximum of seven. Provide methods for shifting and pedaling. Shifting up or down on the front or rear gear changes its value by one, but neither gear can go below one or above its maximum. A pedal action takes no value but calculates the distance traveled in that moment, which is the front gear multiplied by three, plus the rear gear. The entry function `pedal(actions)` takes a list of action strings, creates the transmission, and processes each action. Valid strings are up front, down front, up rear, down rear, and pedal. It accumulates the total distance traveled across all pedal actions. Return a tuple of the total distance traveled and another tuple containing the final front and rear gears.

title: Microscope Stage Controller
spec: Model a microscope stage that tracks its horizontal position, vertical position, magnification, and focus level. The horizontal and vertical positions start at zero, magnification starts at ten, and focus starts at zero. Provide methods for moving, magnifying, and focusing. Moving takes a direction string of either horizontal or vertical and an integer amount, adding the amount to the respective position. Every time a position changes, the focus level drops by the absolute value of the movement amount. Magnifying sets the magnification to a given integer, which cannot go below one. Focusing sets the focus level directly to a given integer. The entry function `examine(movements)` takes a list of tuples containing an action string and a value. It instantiates the stage, applies the movements in sequence, and returns a tuple of the final horizontal, vertical, magnification, and focus values.

title: Cash Register Drawer
spec: Model a cash register drawer that tracks a cash balance starting at fifty and a sales count starting at zero. Provide methods for sales, refunds, and deposits. A sale method takes an amount, adds it to the cash balance, and increases the sales count by one. A refund method takes an amount, subtracts it from the cash balance, and decreases the sales count by one; however, if the refund would drop the cash balance below zero, the transaction is rejected entirely and nothing changes. A deposit method adds an amount to the cash balance without altering the sales count. The entry function `transact(operations)` takes a list of tuples, each with an operation string and an integer amount, processes them using the drawer model, and returns a tuple of the final cash balance and sales count. Example: a sale of twenty followed by a refund of eighty leaves the balance at seventy and count at one, because the refund is rejected.

title: Guitar Amplifier Stack
spec: Model a guitar amplifier that tracks settings for volume, treble, and bass, all initialized to five, along with an overdrive boolean starting as false and a wear counter starting at zero. Provide methods to adjust these settings. Methods for volume, treble, and bass take a target value and set the respective attribute, keeping it bounded strictly between zero and ten inclusive. An overdrive method takes an integer, setting the overdrive state to true if the integer is one, and false otherwise. Every time any of these four adjustment methods is called, the wear counter increases by one. The entry function `play(adjustments)` takes a list of tuples with a control string and a target integer. It creates the amplifier, applies each adjustment by calling the appropriate method, and returns a tuple containing the final volume, treble, bass, overdrive state, and wear counter.

title: Power Loom Mechanism
spec: Model a power loom that tracks a thread count initialized to one thousand, a pattern index starting at zero, and a woven cloth length starting at zero. Provide methods to manage the loom. A thread method takes an amount and adds it to the thread count. A pattern method sets the pattern index to the provided value. A weave method takes a number of rows; for each row, it attempts to consume an amount of thread equal to the pattern index plus one. If enough thread is available, it decreases the thread count and increases the cloth length by one. If there is not enough thread, weaving stops immediately for that specific command. The entry function `weave(actions)` receives a list of tuples containing a command string and an integer, runs them through the loom, and returns a tuple of the final cloth length and remaining thread count.

title: Bookbinding Press Machine
spec: Model a book press that tracks applied pressure starting at fifty, glue temperature starting at one hundred, and a total of books bound starting at zero. Provide methods to adjust settings and press books. A pressure method and a temperature method each simply set their respective attribute to the provided integer. A press method takes a batch size integer; a binding is only successful if the current pressure is strictly above forty and the temperature is strictly above ninety. If successful, the total books bound increases by the batch size, and the pressure drops by the batch size as the machine loosens. If conditions are not met, nothing changes. The entry function `bind(batches)` receives a list of tuples with a command string and an integer value, processes them sequentially, and returns a tuple of the final books bound and the final pressure.

title: Street Sweeper Truck
spec: Model a street sweeper that tracks a water tank level starting at one hundred, a brush speed starting at zero, and a debris collected total starting at zero. Provide methods to fill, adjust speed, and drive. A fill method adds a given amount to the water tank. A speed method sets the brush speed. A drive method takes a distance integer; for each unit of distance, it normally collects debris equal to the brush speed and consumes two units of water. If the water tank reaches zero, driving continues to collect debris but at half the rate using integer division, and water stays at zero. The entry function `sweep(routes)` processes a list of tuples containing an action string and an integer, driving or adjusting the sweeper accordingly, and returns a tuple of the total debris collected and the remaining water tank level.

title: Solar Panel Array Manager
spec: Model a solar panel array that maintains its tilt angle starting at zero, a dirt level starting at zero, and total generated energy starting at zero. Provide methods to tilt, gather dust, generate power, and clean. The tilt method changes the angle by a given amount, keeping it clamped between minus ninety and ninety. The dust method increases the dirt level by a given amount. The sun method takes a light intensity. If the absolute angle is exactly zero, energy increases by the intensity. If the absolute angle is between one and forty-five inclusive, energy increases by half the intensity using integer division. If the absolute angle is strictly greater than forty-five, energy increases by a quarter of the intensity using integer division. In all cases, subtract the dirt level from the initial calculated increase, and if the final result is negative, add zero to the total energy instead. The clean method resets the dirt level to zero. The entry function `generate(events)` takes a list of tuples with an action string and an integer, applies them, and returns the total generated energy.

title: Pinball Arcade Bumper
spec: Model a bumper in a pinball machine that tracks a score multiplier starting at one, an active state starting as false, and a total accumulated score starting at zero. Provide methods to change state and register hits. An activate method sets the active state to true, and a deactivate method sets it to false. An upgrade method adds one to the multiplier. A hit method registers a collision; if the bumper is active, it adds ten times the multiplier to the total score. If the bumper is not active, a hit only adds one to the total score. The entry function `bounce(hits)` takes a list of command strings, instantiates the bumper, processes each command in order, and returns the final total score. Example: a sequence of hit, activate, upgrade, and hit yields an initial one point, then twenty points, for a total of twenty-one.

title: Electric Scooter Rental
spec: Model an electric scooter that tracks its battery charge starting at one hundred, a locked state starting as true, and total distance traveled starting at zero. Provide methods to unlock, lock, charge, and drive. The unlock method takes a pin code; if the code is exactly one two three four, the scooter becomes unlocked. The lock method sets the locked state to true. The charge method adds a given amount to the battery, capping the maximum battery at one hundred. The drive method takes a requested distance. If the scooter is unlocked, it travels up to the requested distance or until the battery runs out, whichever comes first. Each unit of distance traveled consumes one unit of battery. Total distance increases by the actual distance traveled. The entry function `ride(actions)` takes a list of tuples with an action string and an integer value, executes them on the scooter, and returns a tuple of the final distance traveled and battery charge.

title: Digital Voting Machine
spec: Model a voting machine that tracks a paper roll length starting at one thousand and a total vote count starting at zero. It also tracks specific votes for a yes option and a no option, both starting at zero. Provide methods to cast yes, cast no, void a ballot, and replace the paper. A yes vote adds one to both the yes count and total count, and decreases paper length by ten. A no vote adds one to the no count and total count, and decreases paper length by ten. A void action just decreases paper length by ten without counting any votes. A replace action resets the paper length to one thousand. If the paper length is strictly less than ten, attempts to vote or void do nothing at all. The entry function `vote(ballots)` takes a list of action strings, processes them, and returns a tuple of the yes count, no count, and remaining paper length.

title: Professional Fireworks Launcher
spec: Model a fireworks launcher that tracks a safety lock starting as true, a fuse delay starting at five, and a total count of launched fireworks starting at zero. Provide methods to manipulate the launcher. An unlock method sets the safety lock to false, while a lock method sets it to true. A delay method sets the fuse delay to a provided integer. A fire method takes a quantity integer; if the safety is false, it increases the launched count by the quantity and returns a list containing the string boom repeated exactly quantity times. If the safety is true, it returns an empty list. The entry function `launch(sequence)` takes a list of tuples with an action string and an integer, applies them to the launcher, and accumulates all returned boom strings into a single master list. It returns a tuple of the total launched count and this master list.

title: Mechanical Cuckoo Clock
spec: Model a mechanical cuckoo clock that tracks total minutes passed starting at zero, a bird visible state starting as false, and a total chime count starting at zero. Provide methods to advance time and reset the bird. The chime count is always considered to be the total minutes passed divided by sixty, using integer division. An advance method takes an integer of minutes and adds it to the total minutes passed. Whenever an advance causes the calculated chime count to be strictly higher than it was immediately before the advance, the bird visible state becomes true and the chime count updates to the new calculated value. A reset method takes no arguments and pushes the bird back inside, setting the visible state to false. The entry function `tick(events)` takes a list of integers representing minutes passed, with a special case where a negative one means the user activates the reset method instead of advancing time. It applies these events and returns a tuple of the final chime count and bird visible state.

title: Archery Range Target Track
spec: Model an archery target track that maintains a target distance starting at ten, a bullseye count starting at zero, and a total arrows shot count starting at zero. Provide methods to move the target, register a shot, and reset scores. The move method sets the target distance to a given value, strictly bounded to remain between five and fifty inclusive. The shoot method takes an accuracy score from zero to one hundred; it always increases the total arrows count by one. If the accuracy score is strictly greater than the current distance plus fifty, the shot is a bullseye and the bullseye count increases by one. The reset method changes both the bullseye count and total arrows count back to zero. The entry function `shoot(arrows)` processes a list of tuples containing an action string and an integer, applies the actions, and returns a tuple of the final bullseye count and total arrows shot.

title: Swimming Pool Diving Board
spec: Model a diving board that tracks a fulcrum position starting at zero, a bounce count starting at zero, and a broken state starting as false. Provide methods to adjust the fulcrum and perform a jump. The adjust method changes the fulcrum position by adding a given value, but the overall position is clamped to remain between zero and ten inclusive. The jump method takes a diver weight integer. If the weight multiplied by the fulcrum position is strictly greater than five hundred, the board's broken state becomes true. If the board does not break, the bounce count increases by one. If the board is already broken, calling adjust or jump has no effect whatsoever. The entry function `dive(jumps)` receives a list of tuples with an action string and an integer value, executes the sequence, and returns a tuple of the final bounce count and the broken state boolean.

title: Helicopter Rotor Assembly
spec: Model a helicopter rotor system that tracks blade pitch starting at zero, rotational speed starting at zero, and an engine temperature starting at fifty. Provide methods to adjust pitch, apply throttle, and run over time. The pitch method sets the blade pitch, constrained to be between zero and ten inclusive. The throttle method adds a given value to the speed, capping the maximum speed at one hundred. The run method takes a time integer in minutes; the engine temperature increases by the product of speed, pitch, and time, divided by one hundred using integer division. If the temperature ever exceeds one hundred, the speed immediately drops to zero due to an automatic safety shutoff. The entry function `fly(inputs)` takes a list of tuples with an action string and an integer, processes them in order, and returns a tuple of the final speed and temperature.

title: Soft Serve Ice Cream Machine
spec: Model an ice cream machine that tracks a mix level starting at one hundred, a freezing cylinder temperature starting at twenty, and a total servings count starting at zero. Provide methods to cool, refill, and serve. The cool method takes a number of minutes and decreases the temperature by twice that amount of minutes, stopping at a hard minimum temperature of negative ten. The refill method adds a given amount to the mix level. The serve method takes a portion size integer; if the temperature is strictly below zero and the mix level is greater than or equal to the portion size, the mix level decreases by the portion size and the total servings count increases by one. If these conditions are not met, the serve attempt fails and nothing changes. The entry function `dispense(orders)` takes a list of tuples with an action string and an integer, applies them, and returns a tuple of the total servings count and remaining mix level.

title: Hot Air Balloon Navigator
spec: Model a hot air balloon that tracks burner fuel starting at fifty, altitude starting at zero, and horizontal distance starting at zero. Provide methods to burn fuel, cool the envelope, and drift. The burn method takes an amount; it consumes that much fuel and increases altitude by the consumed amount multiplied by ten. If the requested amount is greater than the available fuel, it only burns what is left. The cool method takes a value and decreases altitude by that value, preventing the altitude from ever dropping below zero. The drift method takes a wind speed; it increases the horizontal distance by the wind speed multiplied by the altitude, divided by one hundred using integer division. The entry function `navigate(commands)` takes a list of tuples containing an action string and an integer, runs the balloon model, and returns a tuple of the final altitude and horizontal distance.

title: Heavy Duty Plumbing Valve
spec: Model a heavy duty plumbing valve that tracks internal pressure starting at fifty, an open state starting as false, and total water volume passed starting at zero. Provide methods to toggle, pressurize, and run water. The toggle method flips the open state to its logical opposite. The pressurize method adds a given value to the internal pressure, capping it at a strict maximum of one hundred. The run method takes a duration in seconds; if the valve is currently open, the total volume passed increases by the duration multiplied by the current pressure. Regardless of the open state, running the system causes the internal pressure to drop by the duration, down to a minimum pressure of zero. The entry function `flow(commands)` processes a list of tuples with an action string and an integer, manipulating the valve accordingly, and returns the total water volume passed.

title: Debate Tournament Timer
spec: Model a debate timer that tracks a current speaker integer starting at one, a time total for speaker one starting at zero, and a time total for speaker two starting at zero. It also tracks a penalty flag starting as false. Provide methods to switch speakers and record speaking time. A switch method simply changes the current speaker from one to two, or from two to one. A speak method takes a duration integer and adds it to the time total of whichever speaker is currently active. If either speaker's time total is strictly greater than one hundred at the end of a speak action, the penalty flag is set to true. The entry function `debate(turns)` takes a list of tuples with an action string and an integer. For switch actions, the integer is ignored. It processes the turns sequentially and returns a tuple containing speaker one's time, speaker two's time, and the penalty flag boolean.

title: Radio Transmission Tower
spec: Model a radio broadcasting tower that maintains a frequency starting at ninety, a transmission volume starting at five, and a total listeners count starting at zero. Provide methods to tune, adjust volume, and transmit. The tune method changes the frequency by adding a given value; while the frequency is strictly below eighty, repeatedly add thirty to it, and while it is strictly above one hundred ten, repeatedly subtract thirty from it. The adjust method changes the volume by a given value, keeping it bounded strictly between zero and ten inclusive. The transmit method takes an estimated audience size; it increases the listeners count by the audience size multiplied by the volume. If the frequency is exactly one hundred, the transmission is perfectly clear and adds an extra fifty listeners. The entry function `broadcast(signals)` processes a list of tuples with an action string and an integer, and returns the final listeners count.

title: Construction Cement Mixer
spec: Model a cement mixer that tracks a drum rotation speed starting at zero, a wetness level starting at zero, and a readiness state starting as false. Provide methods to add water, spin the drum, and tumble the mixture. The water method adds a given amount to the wetness level. The spin method directly sets the rotation speed to a given integer. The tumble method simulates time passing; if the rotation speed is strictly greater than ten and the wetness level is between forty and sixty inclusive, the readiness state becomes true. If the wetness is outside that specific range, tumbling ruins the mix and readiness becomes false. If the speed is ten or lower, readiness does not change at all. The entry function `mix(stages)` takes a list of tuples with an action string and an integer, processes the stages, and returns the final readiness boolean.

title: Mechanical Camera Lens
spec: Model a mechanical camera lens that tracks a focal length starting at fifty, an aperture size starting at four, and a count of successful exposures starting at zero. Provide methods to zoom, adjust aperture, and snap a picture. The zoom method adds a given value to the focal length, enforcing a minimum length of twenty and a maximum of two hundred. The aperture method directly sets the aperture size, enforcing a minimum of one and a maximum of twenty-two. The snap method takes an available light level integer; if the light level divided by the aperture size using integer division is strictly greater than ten, it results in a good exposure and the exposure count increases by one. Otherwise, the shot fails and the count is completely unchanged. The entry function `photograph(settings)` takes a list of tuples with an action string and an integer, applies them to the lens, and returns the exposure count.

title: Artisan Glassblower Pipe
spec: Model a glassblowing pipe that tracks glass temperature starting at one thousand, air volume starting at zero, and shape stability starting at true. Provide methods to heat, blow air, and shape. The heat method increases the temperature by a given amount. The blow method adds a given amount to the air volume. The shape method simulates time spent manipulating the glass, taking a duration integer; the temperature drops by the duration multiplied by ten. If an attempt to shape happens when the temperature is strictly below eight hundred, the glass cracks and the shape stability becomes false. If the air volume ever strictly exceeds fifty during a blow action, the glass bursts and shape stability also becomes false. The entry function `blow(actions)` takes a list of tuples with an action string and an integer, processes them, and returns a tuple of the final air volume, temperature, and stability boolean.

title: Planetary Surface Rover
spec: Write a system to track a planetary rover. The rover starts at origin zero zero facing north, with a battery level of one hundred and an empty sample manifest. It has actions to move forward by a given distance, turn ninety degrees left or right, gather a soil sample of a specific weight, and recharge. Moving consumes one battery unit per distance unit, while gathering a sample consumes five battery units and adds the weight to the total collected. If the battery is insufficient for an action, the rover does nothing for that step. The main entry point `navigate(commands)` receives a list of tuples containing an action string and an integer value, processes them in sequence, and returns a tuple of final horizontal position, vertical position, and total sample weight. Example input: move ten, gather three, turn one.

title: Text Editor Buffer
spec: Simulate a simple line based text buffer. The buffer maintains a list of strings and a current cursor line index starting at zero. Operations include inserting a new line at the cursor, deleting the current line, moving the cursor up or down by a specific number of lines, and replacing the current line text. If moving the cursor exceeds the buffer boundaries, it clamps to the top or bottom, and inserting pushes the current and subsequent lines down. Deleting the only remaining line leaves a single empty string. The entry point `edit(operations)` takes a list of instruction tuples consisting of an operation name and a string or integer argument, applies them to a new buffer, and returns the final text as a single string joined by newlines. Example input: insert hello, insert world, move up one, delete.

title: Emergency Triage Queue
spec: Model a hospital emergency room queue. The queue manages patients waiting for care, categorized by severity from one to five, where one is most critical. Patients arrive with a severity and an estimated treatment duration, or the system can advance time by a given number of minutes, reducing the remaining treatment time of the currently seen patient. If the current patient finishes, the system immediately admits the waiting patient with the highest severity, breaking ties by the longest waiting time. The main function `triage(arrivals)` accepts a list of events which are either patient arrivals represented by severity and duration, or time advancements in minutes. It returns the number of patients still waiting and the severity of the currently treated patient, or zero if no patient is being treated.

title: Cloud Load Balancer
spec: Create a cloud server load balancer manager. The system maintains three servers, each starting with zero active connections and a maximum capacity of ten. When a new request arrives, it is routed to the server with the lowest current connections, breaking ties by picking the server with the lowest numerical identifier. If all servers are at maximum capacity, the request is dropped and counted as a failure. The system can also receive completion signals for a specific server, decreasing its active connection count by one down to a minimum of zero. The entry function `distribute(requests)` processes a list of strings, where each string is either a new request or a completion signal for a specific server identifier. It returns a tuple containing the dropped request count and a list of active connections for servers zero, one, and two.

title: Airline Flight Roster
spec: Implement a flight passenger manager. The flight has a maximum capacity of fifty economy seats and ten first class seats. Passengers can book an economy seat, book a first class seat, or cancel their booking, but if a class is full, the booking fails. The system must also support upgrading an existing economy passenger to first class, which succeeds only if first class has available seats and the passenger holds an economy ticket. The flight keeps track of total revenue, where economy costs two hundred, first class costs five hundred, upgrades add three hundred, and cancellations refund the full amount. The entry function `book(transactions)` processes a list of tuples containing an action name, passenger name, and ticket type. It returns the final revenue and the number of available economy seats.

title: Postal Center Sorter
spec: Simulate a postal sorting center. The center has three regional bins: east for zip codes starting with zero to three, central for four to six, and west for seven to nine, and tracks the total weight of parcels in each. Each parcel has a destination zip code and a weight, and there is a processing limit of fifty total weight units per day. If adding a parcel exceeds the daily weight limit across all bins, it is held back in a backlog queue. A new day action resets the daily weight accumulator and processes as many backlog parcels as possible before taking new ones. The entry function `process(parcels)` takes a list of parcel tuples with zip code and weight, interspersed with new day signals. It returns a tuple of the three bin weights and the number of parcels left in the backlog.

title: RPG Character Inventory
spec: Design a character inventory system. The inventory has a maximum of twenty slots and tracks the current gold pieces. Items can be added to take up one slot each, and if the inventory is full, new items are discarded. Items can be sold, which removes them from the slots and adds their value to the gold total, or dropped, which removes them without gaining gold.
