A player can equip one weapon and one armor piece from their inventory, freeing up the slots they occupied, and if an item is already equipped in that slot, it is returned to the inventory. The entry function `manage(actions)` receives a sequence of action tuples indicating the action, item type, and value. It returns the final gold amount and the number of filled inventory slots.

title: Hydroelectric Dam Control
spec: Model a hydroelectric dam system. The dam tracks its reservoir water level in meters starting at fifty, total generated power in megawatts starting at zero, and whether the spillway gates are open or closed. Rain events add a specific amount to the water level. Every hour, if the water level is above forty, the turbines run, consuming two meters of water and generating ten megawatts. If the level exceeds eighty, the spillway gates automatically open to prevent overflow, releasing five meters of water per hour without generating power, and they close automatically when the level drops below sixty. The main function `operate(events)` accepts a list of integers representing rain amounts per hour. It returns the final water level, the total power generated, and a boolean indicating if the gates are open.

title: Podcast Application Player
spec: Create a podcast player manager. The player maintains a playlist of episode strings and tracks the current episode index and playback timestamp in seconds. Playback commands advance the timestamp by a given number of seconds, and if the timestamp reaches or exceeds three thousand seconds, the current episode ends, the timestamp resets to zero, and the player advances to the next episode. The user can also skip to the next episode manually or jump backwards by fifteen seconds, which clamps the timestamp to zero. The entry function `listen(commands)` processes a list of tuples containing a command string and an optional integer argument. It returns the name of the currently playing episode and the current timestamp, or a string saying finished if the playlist is exhausted.

title: Ferris Wheel Operator
spec: Simulate a Ferris wheel with eight gondolas indexed zero to seven. Each gondola holds up to four people, and the wheel tracks its current bottom position, initially gondola zero. Actions include loading a specific number of people into the bottom gondola, rejecting any excess people beyond the capacity of four, and rotating the wheel by one position to advance the bottom gondola index. A complete revolution tracking variable increments every time gondola zero returns to the bottom. Unloading removes all people from the current bottom gondola and adds them to a total served counter. The entry function `run(actions)` takes a list of actions and returns the total served people and the number of complete revolutions.

title: Vehicle Dashboard
spec: Model a vehicle dashboard. The vehicle tracks its current speed in kilometers per hour, total distance traveled, and fuel level in liters starting at fifty. When the engine is turned on, the driver can accelerate to increase speed by ten, or brake to decrease speed by ten down to zero, with each acceleration consuming one liter of fuel. If fuel reaches zero, the engine turns off and speed drops to zero. A cruise command maintains the current speed and adds the speed value to the total distance, consuming fuel equal to the speed divided by ten. The main function `drive(inputs)` takes a list of command strings like start, stop, accelerate, brake, or cruise. It returns the total distance traveled and the remaining fuel level.

title: Ride Sharing Dispatcher
spec: Implement a ride sharing dispatcher. The system tracks three drivers, each with a current location on a one dimensional road starting at zero, ten, and twenty respectively, and tracks their total earned fares. When a passenger requests a ride from a start coordinate to a destination coordinate, the system assigns the driver who is currently closest to the start coordinate, breaking ties in favor of the driver with the lower identifier. The chosen driver moves to the start coordinate, then to the destination, and earns a fare equal to the distance between start and destination. The entry function `dispatch(requests)` processes a list of passenger request tuples containing start and destination coordinates. It returns a list of the final coordinates of all three drivers and a list of their total earned fares.

title: Subscription Biller
spec: Simulate a subscription billing system. A user account has a tier of basic or premium, a status of active or paused, and a balance of outstanding charges starting at zero. Basic costs ten per month and premium costs twenty, and each month, if the account is active, the tier cost is added to the balance. The user can upgrade to premium, downgrade to basic, pause the account, resume the account, or make a payment of a specific amount to reduce the balance. If the balance ever exceeds fifty after monthly charges, the account is automatically paused due to non payment. The entry function `bill(months)` receives a list of monthly event lists, where each event list contains actions taken before the monthly billing runs. It returns the final balance and the final status of the account.

title: Radar Tracking Array
spec: Design a radar tracking system. The system maintains a collection of tracked airborne objects, each identified by a unique integer, along with their current altitude and distance from the radar. When a scan detects an object, if it is new, it is added to the tracker, and if it already exists, its altitude and distance are updated. The threat level is calculated as altitude divided by distance, and if this exceeds ten, the system issues an alert by incrementing a global alert counter. Objects that are not detected for three consecutive scans are considered lost and removed from the tracker. The entry function `scan(signals)` processes a list of scans, where each scan is a list of detected object tuples with identifier, altitude, and distance. It returns the total number of alerts issued and the number of currently tracked objects.

title: Digital Asset Wallet
spec: Create a digital asset wallet simulator. The wallet holds a primary coin balance and a collection of secondary tokens, and every transaction requires a network fee of one primary coin. The user can receive primary coins or tokens without paying a fee, but sending tokens deducts the token amount and the primary coin fee. Swapping tokens exchanges a given amount of one token for another at a one to one ratio, consuming the fee. If the primary balance is too low to cover the fee, or if a transaction attempts to send or swap more tokens than available, the transaction fails entirely. The main function `transact(operations)` accepts an initial primary coin balance and a list of operation tuples containing action, asset name, amount, and an optional second asset. It returns the final primary coin balance and the final balance of a token named star.

title: Cash Dispenser Machine
spec: Model a cash machine that holds a physical inventory of twenty, fifty, and hundred denomination bills, initially stocked with ten of each. A user inserts a card with a known account balance and can request a withdrawal of a specific amount. The machine attempts to dispense the amount using the largest bills possible, and if the machine lacks the exact bills to make the requested amount or the user balance is insufficient, the withdrawal is rejected. If successful, the user balance and the machine inventory are updated accordingly. The user can also deposit bills, increasing their balance and the machine inventory. The entry function `dispense(transactions)` takes an initial user balance and a list of action tuples containing the action type and an amount or list of deposited bills. It returns the final user balance and the total count of bills remaining in the machine.

title: Factory Sorting Conveyor
spec: Implement a factory sorting mechanism. A conveyor belt moves items, each having a weight and a color, past three robotic arms: one for red items, one for blue items, and a heavy lifter. The heavy lifter intercepts any item weighing more than fifty units regardless of color and places it in a bulk bin, otherwise the red arm picks red items and the blue arm picks blue items. Any other colors or items that the arms miss fall off the end into a reject bin. The red and blue arms require a cool down of one step after picking an item, meaning they cannot pick an item on the very next conveyor step. The main function `sort(items)` processes a list of item tuples containing color and weight. It returns the count of items in the bulk bin, red bin, blue bin, and reject bin.

title: Playing Card Deck
spec: Simulate a simple card drawing game. The deck contains integers from one to fifty in order, and a hand holds up to five cards. The player can draw a card from the top of the deck to their hand, and if the hand is full, the drawn card is immediately placed in a discard pile. The player can also play the highest card from their hand, adding its value to their score and moving it to the discard pile. If the deck runs out, a shuffle action takes all cards from the discard pile, reverses their order, and makes them the new deck. The entry function `play(moves)` accepts a list of player moves as strings like draw, play, or shuffle. It returns the player score and the number of cards remaining in the deck.

title: Deep Space Probe
spec: Write a controller for a deep space probe operating on a two dimensional grid. The probe starts at coordinates zero zero facing east and has a solar panel that collects one energy unit every time it moves. Moving forward one space consumes two energy units, turning left or right consumes one energy unit, and performing a scan of its current sector consumes five energy units while adding the sector coordinates to a discovered list. If energy drops to zero, the probe enters sleep mode and ignores all commands until it receives a special wait command, which restores ten energy. The probe starts with twenty energy. The entry function `explore(commands)` takes a list of command strings. It returns the final energy level and the number of sectors scanned.

title: Railway Switch Yard
spec: Model a railway switching yard. The yard has a main incoming track and three holding tracks numbered one, two, and three. Trains arrive on the main track with a destination code and a car count, and the switch operator routes the train to a holding track. Track one holds up to twenty cars, track two holds thirty, and track three holds ten. If a routed train exceeds the remaining car capacity of the chosen track, it is instead sent to a bypass track. The yard can also dispatch a train from a holding track, completely emptying that track and freeing its capacity. The entry function `route(instructions)` processes a list of instructions, which are either arrivals with destination, car count, and target track, or dispatches with the track number. It returns the total number of cars sent to the bypass track and the remaining capacity of track two.

title: Freight Delivery Truck
spec: Simulate a freight delivery truck. The truck has a cargo capacity of five thousand kilograms and a fuel tank of one hundred gallons, starting fully fueled at the depot. The truck loads packages with destinations and weights, and if loading a package exceeds the weight capacity, it is left at the depot. The truck travels to destinations, consuming one gallon of fuel per mile. Upon reaching a destination, all packages for that destination are unloaded, freeing up weight capacity. If the truck lacks enough fuel to reach the next destination, it stops and calls for a tow. The entry function `deliver(manifest)` receives a list of loading actions containing destination and weight, and travel actions containing destination and distance in miles. It returns the total weight of unloaded packages and the remaining fuel.

title: Museum Tour Group
spec: Create a system to manage a museum tour group. The tour guide starts with a group of zero visitors in the lobby, and visitors can join or leave the group at any time. The guide moves the group through various rooms: the lobby, the ancient history hall, the art gallery, and the science wing. The ancient history hall allows twenty people, the art gallery allows fifteen, and the science wing allows thirty. If the guide tries to move the group into a room and the group size exceeds the room occupancy, they must wait in the current room until enough visitors leave. The tour earns a tip of one dollar per person every time they successfully enter a new room. The main function `tour(events)` accepts a list of events like join count, leave count, or move to room. It returns the total tips earned and the final room the group is in.

title: Mountain Cable Car
spec: Design a mountain cable car system. There are two stations called base and summit, and the cable car holds up to forty passengers, starting at the base station. Passengers arrive at either station and join a waiting queue. When the cable car departs, it boards as many waiting passengers as possible up to its capacity from its current station, and travels to the other station. Upon arrival, all boarded passengers exit, completing a trip that takes fifteen minutes. The system tracks the current time in minutes, starting at zero. The entry function `transport(schedule)` processes a list of events which are either passenger arrivals at a specific station with a number of people, or dispatch commands. It returns the total number of passengers transported and the number of people left waiting at the base station queue.

title: Strategy Board Game
spec: Implement the logic for a simplified strategy board game. Two players, black and white, start with ten pieces each, and the board has five zones. Each turn, a player can deploy pieces to a zone or attack an opponent in a zone. Deploying adds pieces from the player reserve to the zone. Attacking compares the number of pieces the attacker and defender have in the zone; if the attacker has more pieces, the defender loses all pieces in that zone and the attacker loses half of their attacking pieces, rounded down. If the defender has equal or more pieces, the attack fails and the attacker loses all pieces in the zone. The entry function `battle(turns)` takes a list of turn tuples containing player color, action, zone, and amount. It returns the final total number of surviving pieces on the board for black and for white.

title: Predator Prey Grid
spec: Model a simple predator and prey ecosystem on a one dimensional grid of ten cells. Cells can be empty, or hold a plant, a herbivore, or a carnivore. Plants grow in empty cells automatically every three cycles. Herbivores eat plants, gaining one energy point, and move to an adjacent cell if possible. Carnivores eat herbivores, gaining two energy points, and move. If an animal goes three cycles without eating, it dies and its cell becomes empty, and animals cannot move beyond the boundaries of the grid. The main function `simulate(cycles)` initializes a specific grid state and processes a number of simulated time cycles. Given a list of initial placements containing index and entity type, it runs the cycles and returns a count of surviving herbivores and carnivores.

title: Gymnasium Access Control
spec: A class manages a member's facility access, maintaining their current membership status, remaining guest passes, and outstanding balance. A method processes a facility check in, denying entry if the balance exceeds fifty dollars or if the status is inactive, otherwise recording a successful visit. Another method adds a charge to the balance for purchasing drinks or towels. A third method handles guest admissions, deducting from the remaining guest passes if available or adding a twenty dollar fee to the balance if none remain. The entry function `process(actions)` processes a list of action tuples containing the action type and an optional value, and returns a tuple of the final balance, remaining passes, and total successful visits. For example, processing a check in, a charge of ten, and a guest admission returns a balance of ten, four guest passes, and one visit.

title: Commercial Washing Machine
spec: A class controls a heavy duty laundromat washer by tracking the door lock status, current water temperature, remaining detergent ounces, and drum rotation speed. A method handles adding detergent, increasing the supply up to a maximum of thirty ounces. A second method sets the cycle mode, locking the door, setting the water temperature to cold, warm, or hot based on the fabric requirement, and engaging the drum at a specific rotation speed. A third method advances the timer, stopping the drum and unlocking the door when finished. The entry function `wash(cycles)` receives a list of instruction tuples and executes them in sequence, returning a list of the final machine states after each step. For example, adding ten detergent and starting a warm cycle results in the state showing ten ounces, a locked door, and warm water.

title: Campsite Ledger
spec: A class represents a wilderness campsite booking by maintaining the current occupant name, the number of nights reserved, the fire pit rental status, and the damage deposit amount. A booking method assigns the camper name, sets the nights, and clears any previous damage flags. Another method extends the stay by adding nights to the current reservation. A third method flags property damage, which nullifies the damage deposit and records an eviction notice. The entry function `manage(requests)` evaluates a list of request strings and their corresponding integer arguments, applying them to the campsite and returning a summary sentence of the current occupant, total nights, and deposit status. For example, booking for three nights and extending by two results in a summary stating the site is occupied for five nights with a full deposit.

title: Filament Extruder Head
spec: A class models a three dimensional printer nozzle by tracking its current temperature, the loaded filament material, the nozzle position on the horizontal axis, and the amount of plastic extruded. A heating method increases the temperature to match the required melting point of the loaded material. A movement method updates the nozzle position and, if the temperature is high enough, adds to the total extruded plastic based on the distance moved. A cooling method drops the temperature back to ambient levels to prevent burning. The entry function `fabricate(commands)` accepts a list of command tuples to change material, heat, move, or cool, and returns the final temperature, position, and total extruded volume. For example, heating up and moving ten units results in a positive extrusion volume and a new position.

title: Plasma Donation Cooler
spec: A class manages a medical storage cooler by tracking the internal temperature, the current inventory count of plasma bags, the alert buzzer status, and the door open duration. An insertion method adds to the inventory and briefly increases the internal temperature by two degrees. A monitoring method checks if the temperature exceeds negative ten degrees or if the door has been open for more than five minutes, activating the alert buzzer if true. A maintenance method resets the buzzer and rapidly cools the internal temperature back to negative twenty degrees. The entry function `refrigerate(events)` reads a sequence of event types and numeric values, applies them to the cooler, and returns the final inventory count and buzzer status. For example, adding three bags and leaving the door open for six minutes returns an inventory of three with an active alert buzzer.

title: Industrial Citrus Press
spec: A class operates a large scale fruit press by keeping track of the hydraulic pressure setting, the total gallons of juice extracted, the pulp bin capacity, and the safety guard status. A preparation method engages the safety guard and sets the pressure based on the fruit type, using high pressure for grapefruits and low for tangerines. A pressing method extracts juice, adding to the total gallons and increasing the pulp bin fill level. A cleaning method disengages the guard, resets the pressure, and empties the pulp bin. The entry function `juice(batches)` applies a sequence of batch descriptions to the press and returns the total gallons extracted and the final pulp bin level. For example, pressing a batch of grapefruits and then emptying the bin returns the juice volume and a zero pulp level.

title: Craft Beer Fermenter
spec: A class monitors a brewery vessel by recording the current specific gravity of the liquid, the ambient cooling jacket temperature, the internal carbon dioxide pressure, and the yeast activity level. A pitching method introduces yeast, increasing the activity level and dropping the cooling jacket temperature to a baseline. A daily reading method simulates the passage of time by decreasing the specific gravity, increasing the internal pressure, and altering the yeast activity. A venting method releases excess carbon dioxide pressure once it reaches a critical safety threshold. The entry function `ferment(stages)` processes a list of daily action codes, updating the vessel state, and returns the final specific gravity and pressure readings. For example, pitching yeast followed by three daily readings results in a lower specific gravity and increased pressure.

title: Passenger Ferry Ramp
spec: A class controls a vehicle boarding ramp for a harbor ferry by maintaining the ramp elevation angle, the securing latch status, the hydraulic fluid level, and the count of loaded vehicles. A deployment method lowers the elevation angle to zero degrees and disengages the securing latch. A boarding method increments the vehicle count and slightly depletes the hydraulic fluid level as the ramp adjusts to the shifting weight. A stowage method raises the ramp back to ninety degrees and engages the securing latch for departure. The entry function `board(operations)` receives a list of operation codes to deploy, board, or stow, and returns the final vehicle count, latch status, and elevation angle. For example, deploying the ramp and boarding five vehicles returns a count of five, an open latch, and a zero degree angle.

title: Ice Resurfacing Tractor
spec: A class simulates a skating rink maintenance vehicle by tracking the fresh water tank volume, the snow collection bin level, the cutting blade depth, and the battery charge. A calibration method sets the blade depth based on the roughness of the ice and ensures the battery has sufficient charge to begin. A driving method simulates completing a lap around the rink, which uses water to smooth the surface, fills the snow bin with shaved ice, and drains battery power. A dumping method empties the snow collection bin and refills the water tank. The entry function `resurface(laps)` evaluates a list of lap instructions and maintenance actions, returning the remaining battery charge, water volume, and snow bin level. For example, driving two laps and then dumping the snow returns a full water tank, an empty snow bin, and a depleted battery charge.

title: Open Pit Excavator
spec: A class represents a heavy mining shovel by tracking the diesel fuel level, the current bucket payload weight, the engine operating temperature, and the total tons moved. A digging method scoops material, adding weight to the bucket and raising the engine temperature slightly. A dumping method empties the bucket into a haul truck, adding the payload to the total tons moved and consuming diesel fuel. A resting method allows the engine temperature to return to normal and refuels the diesel tank if it is critically low. The entry function `excavate(shifts)` applies a sequence of shift commands to the shovel and returns the total tons moved and the final engine temperature. For example, digging twice, dumping, and resting results in a recorded payload transfer and a normal engine temperature.

title: Overnight Train Sleeper
spec: A class manages a luxury railway sleeper car by keeping track of the berth status, the morning tea requirement, the dining car tab, and the attendant call button. A boarding method marks the berth as occupied, flags it for morning tea, and opens a new dining car tab. A dining method adds meal costs to the dining car tab when the passenger orders food. A service method clears the tea flag and resets the attendant call button after the conductor visits. The entry function `accommodate(demands)` processes a series of passenger actions and staff visits, returning the final dining car tab and call button status. For example, boarding followed by two meals and an attendant visit results in a positive tab and a reset call button.

title: Planetarium Projector System
spec: A class operates a star projector by maintaining the current lens focus, the light bulb intensity, the rotation speed of the star sphere, and the cooling fan status. A startup method sets the light bulb intensity to maximum, engages the cooling fan, and initializes the lens focus to a default wide angle. A transition method adjusts the rotation speed and refines the lens focus to highlight specific constellations. A shutdown method turns off the bulb, stops the rotation, and keeps the fan running for a brief cooldown period before stopping it. The entry function `project(shows)` takes a list of show commands, applies them to the projector, and returns the final lens focus, bulb intensity, and fan status. For example, starting up and transitioning to a fast rotation returns a wide focus, maximum intensity, and an active fan.

title: Laser Skirmish Vest
spec: A class models a wearable gaming vest by tracking the player health points, the team color assignment, the remaining ammunition, and the vibration motor state. An initialization method sets the team color, provides full health points, and grants a starting supply of ammunition. A firing method decreases the remaining ammunition and triggers a brief vibration if the shot is successful. A receiving method reduces the health points when hit by an opponent and activates a sustained vibration, deactivating the vest entirely if health reaches zero. The entry function `play(hits)` reads a sequence of game events, updates the vest accordingly, and returns a tuple of the final health points and ammunition count. For example, initializing a red team vest, firing twice, and receiving one hit returns reduced health and slightly depleted ammunition.

title: Blast Furnace Blower
spec: A class monitors an industrial metallurgy blower by recording the current airflow rate, the target core temperature, the emergency bypass status, and the total oxygen delivered. An adjustment method changes the airflow rate based on incoming temperature data, blowing harder if the core is too cold and restricting if it becomes too hot. A delivery method updates the total oxygen delivered based on the current airflow over a time interval. A safety method engages the emergency bypass and sets the airflow rate to zero if the temperature exceeds critical structural limits. The entry function `smelt(readings)` processes a list of temperature readings, adjusting the blower for each, and returns the total oxygen delivered and the emergency bypass status. For example, processing three normal readings and one critical spike results in halted airflow and an active bypass.

title: Recovery Vehicle Winch
spec: A class operates a tow truck cable system by tracking the unspooled cable length, the attached load weight, the drum brake status, and the motor temperature. A release method disengages the drum brake and increases the unspooled cable length to reach a stranded vehicle. A hooking method secures the vehicle by updating the attached load weight and engaging the drum brake. A pulling method reels in the cable, decreasing its length while significantly raising the motor temperature based on the load weight. The entry function `tow(pulls)` accepts a sequence of winching operations, applies them to the system, and returns the final cable length and motor temperature. For example, releasing fifty units of cable, hooking a heavy load, and pulling twenty units returns a length of thirty and an elevated temperature.

title: Indoor Rowing Machine
spec: A class simulates an exercise ergometer by maintaining the magnetic resistance level, the accumulated distance, the current stroke rate, and the estimated calories burned. A setup method configures the resistance level based on the user preference and resets the distance and calories to zero. A pulling method processes individual strokes, adding to the accumulated distance and calculating calories burned based on the resistance and stroke intensity. A pacing method adjusts the current stroke rate based on the time elapsed between recent pulls. The entry function `row(strokes)` evaluates a list of stroke intensities and time intervals, returning the total distance and calories burned. For example, completing a setup and twenty vigorous pulls results in a high calorie count and significant distance covered.

title: Casino Slot Reel
spec: A class represents a mechanical gambling device by tracking the current jackpot pool, the displayed symbols on the payline, the internal coin hopper balance, and the payout multiplier. A wager method accepts a bet, adding it to the jackpot pool and increasing the hopper balance. A spinning method randomizes the displayed symbols and calculates a potential win based on matching items and the current multiplier. A payout method dispenses coins from the hopper if a win occurs and resets the jackpot pool if the grand prize is hit. The entry function `spin(wagers)` takes a list of betting amounts and spin outcomes, updates the machine state, and returns the final hopper balance and jackpot pool. For example, placing three wagers and hitting a minor payout returns a slightly lower hopper balance and a growing jackpot.

title: Tower Crane Boom
spec: A class controls a construction lifting machine by tracking the hook elevation, the trolley position along the arm, the suspended payload mass, and the wind speed warning flag. A lifting method raises or lowers the hook elevation, checking that the payload mass does not exceed the safe lifting limit. A traversing method moves the trolley closer to or further from the central mast, adjusting the safe lifting limit based on the distance. A weather method updates the wind speed warning flag, halting all movement if the wind is too strong. The entry function `hoist(movements)` processes a sequence of movement directives and weather updates, returning the final hook elevation and trolley position. For example, lifting a moderate payload and traversing outwards during calm weather returns the new vertical and horizontal coordinates.

title: Bascule Bridge Mechanism
spec: A class manages a movable river crossing by tracking the span elevation angle, the road barrier status, the marine traffic queue, and the structural lock engagement. A halting method closes the road barriers to vehicle traffic and disengages the structural locks. A raising method increases the span elevation angle to allow marine vessels to pass and decrements the marine traffic queue as boats clear the area. A lowering method returns the span to a zero degree angle, engages the structural locks, and opens the road barriers. The entry function `operate(signals)` interprets a list of traffic signals, updating the bridge state, and returns the final elevation angle and marine traffic queue size. For example, halting traffic, raising the bridge for two waiting boats, and lowering it returns a zero angle and an empty queue.

title: Wool Spinning Wheel
spec: A class models a traditional textile tool by tracking the spindle rotation speed, the tension of the drive band, the accumulated yarn yardage, and the bobbin fill level. A pedaling method increases the spindle rotation speed and consumes raw wool to add to the yarn yardage. A tensioning method tightens or loosens the drive band, which adjusts how quickly the spun yarn is wound onto the bobbin. A winding method transfers the accumulated yarn to the bobbin, increasing its fill level and stopping the process if the bobbin becomes completely full. The entry function `weave(steps)` evaluates a sequence of pedaling, tensioning, and winding actions, returning the final yarn yardage and bobbin fill level. For example, fast pedaling with high tension quickly produces and stores yarn, resulting in a partially full bobbin.

title: Canopy Tour Braking System
spec: A class monitors a zip line safety mechanism by recording the rider velocity, the brake pad wear percentage, the cable tension, and the arrival platform status. A launching method sets the initial rider velocity and increases the cable tension based on the weight of the person. A braking method applies friction, rapidly decreasing the rider velocity while increasing the brake pad wear percentage. A resetting method clears the arrival platform and restores the cable tension to its resting baseline. The entry function `descend(riders)` processes a list of rider weights and braking durations, applying them to the system, and returns the final brake pad wear and cable tension. For example, launching a heavy rider and applying a long brake duration results in high brake wear and a safe arrival.

title: Commercial Truck Tire Monitor
spec: A class tracks a long haul vehicle sensor system by maintaining the current internal air pressure, the tread temperature, the total mileage driven, and the slow leak warning flag. A driving method adds to the total mileage, slightly increases the tread temperature, and simulates normal air pressure loss over long distances. A resting method allows the tread temperature to cool down to ambient levels. A diagnostic method evaluates the pressure drop over time, setting the slow leak warning flag if the loss exceeds a safety threshold. The entry function `monitor(journeys)` accepts a sequence of driving distances and resting periods, updating the tire state, and returns the final air pressure and warning flag status. For example, driving a long distance without resting triggers a temperature spike and potentially a leak warning.

title: Reverse Osmosis Purifier
spec: A class controls a water desalination unit by tracking the intake salinity level, the membrane pressure gauge, the fresh water output volume, and the filter backwash requirement. A pumping method applies high pressure to the membrane and extracts fresh water, increasing the output volume based on the pressure applied. A sensing method updates the intake salinity level, which requires the system to adjust the membrane pressure to maintain efficiency. A flushing method performs a filter backwash, cleaning the membrane and resetting the backwash requirement flag. The entry function `purify(intervals)` processes a sequence of operation cycles and maintenance triggers, returning the total fresh water output and the final membrane pressure. For example, processing high salinity water requires higher pressure and frequent flushing to maintain fresh water output.

title: Hardware Store Paint Mixer
spec: A class operates a custom color dispensing machine by keeping track of the white base paint volume, the levels of red, blue, and yellow colorant, and the current mixing nozzle status. A base method loads a specific volume of white paint into the mixing can. A tinting method dispenses precise fractions of the primary colorants into the can, deducting from their respective storage levels. A blending method engages the mixing nozzle to combine the ingredients, then flags the nozzle as requiring a cleaning cycle. The entry function `tint(formulas)` takes a list of color formulas, processes them sequentially, and returns the remaining colorant levels and the total cans mixed. For example, loading a base and tinting with equal parts red and blue produces a purple mix and slightly depletes the respective colorants.

title: Vintage Neon Transformer
spec: A class manages a classic electrical sign by tracking the input voltage, the internal gas pressure, the tube temperature, and the flickering state. A powering method supplies input voltage, which excites the gas and slowly raises the tube temperature. A dimming method reduces the voltage, allowing the temperature to fall but potentially triggering the flickering state if the voltage drops too low. A fault method detects if the tube temperature exceeds a safe maximum, completely cutting the voltage to prevent shattered glass. The entry function `illuminate(patterns)` interprets a list of lighting pattern commands, applying them to the sign, and returns the final tube temperature and flickering state. For example, applying high voltage for a long duration followed by a sharp drop results in a high temperature and a flickering sign.

title: Bread Toaster Controller
spec: The entry function is `toast(actions)`. Create a toaster object with a brownness dial starting at three, a lever state initially up, and a crumb tray holding zero grams. Create a separate heating element object that tracks its current temperature and whether it is active. When receiving a push action, the lever goes down and the heating element activates. A dial action followed by a number sets the dial to that level. A pop action deactivates the heating element, moves the lever up, and adds crumbs equal to the dial level multiplied by two. A clean action resets the crumbs to zero. Process a list of actions and return a tuple with the final lever state, the active status of the heater, and total crumbs. Example input: ["push", "dial 5", "pop"]. Output: ("up", False, 10).

title: Geothermal Heat Pump
spec: The entry function is `regulate(readings)`. Build a pump system that manages a ground loop and an indoor fan. The ground loop maintains a fluid pressure initially at fifty and a valve status initially closed. The fan tracks its speed initially zero. For each temperature reading in the input list, if the reading is below sixty, open the ground loop valve, increase the pressure by ten, and set the fan speed to high. If the reading is above seventy, close the valve, decrease the pressure by five, and set the fan speed to medium. For readings in between, close the valve and set the fan speed to low. The ground loop pressure must never exceed eighty or drop below twenty. Return a list of tuples representing the valve status, pressure, and fan speed after each reading. Example input: [55, 75]. Output: [("open", 60, "high"), ("closed", 55, "medium")].

title: Maple Syrup Evaporator
spec: The entry function is `boil(steps)`. Construct an evaporator system containing a main pan and a sap reservoir. The reservoir holds an initial volume of one hundred. The main pan tracks its temperature starting at sixty and sugar concentration starting at two. Process a sequence of text steps. A heat step increases temperature by thirty and, if temperature is at or above two hundred, increases sugar concentration by ten. A fill step subtracts fifteen from the reservoir volume and decreases temperature by ten. A draw step reduces the concentration by fifty if it is above fifty. Return a tuple containing the final reservoir volume, pan temperature, and sugar concentration. Example input: ["heat", "heat", "heat", "heat", "heat"]. Output: (100, 210, 12).

title: Bouncy Castle Monitor
spec: The entry function is `monitor(events)`. Manage a bouncy castle and an air blower. The castle tracks current kids starting at zero and a seam stress level starting at zero. The air blower has a power level starting at normal and an overheat flag initially false. Process a list of events. An enter event adds one to kids and increases stress by five. An exit event reduces kids by one and decreases stress by three. A bounce event increases stress by ten. After each event, update the air blower: if stress exceeds fifty, set power to high and overheat to true; if stress is between thirty and fifty, set power to medium and overheat to false; otherwise set it to normal and false. Return the final kid count, stress level, and blower power. Example input: ["enter", "enter", "bounce"]. Output: (2, 20, "normal").

title: Cheese Cave Humidifier
spec: The entry function is `condition(measurements)`. Create a humidifier object and a ventilation fan object to maintain a cheese cave. The humidifier starts at a water level of one hundred and is initially off. The fan starts at zero speed. Iterate through a list of humidity measurements. If a measurement is below eighty, turn the humidifier on, consume five units of water, and set fan speed to low. If a measurement is above ninety, turn the humidifier off and set the fan speed to high to dry the air. If between eighty and ninety, turn the humidifier off and set fan speed to low. If water level hits zero, the humidifier cannot turn on. Return the final water level, humidifier state, and fan speed. Example input: [70, 95, 85]. Output: (95, False, "low").

title: Go Kart Track Timing
spec: The entry function is `race(laps)`. Track the state of a go kart and its current race session. The kart tracks its fuel level starting at ten and tire wear starting at zero. The session tracks the fastest lap time initially nine hundred ninety nine and total laps completed initially zero. Process a list of lap times. For each time, increase tire wear by two and decrease fuel by one. If tire wear exceeds ten, add five seconds to the lap time. If the adjusted lap time is less than the fastest lap, update the fastest lap. If fuel reaches zero, stop processing further laps. Return a tuple of total laps completed, the fastest lap time, fuel remaining, and tire wear. Example input: [40, 38, 42]. Output: (3, 38, 7, 6).

title: Hot Tub Sanitizer
spec: The entry function is `sanitize(actions)`. Model a hot tub with a chlorine dispenser and a filter cycle. The hot tub tracks its cleanliness initially one hundred and its water volume initially five hundred. The dispenser tracks its chemical reserve initially fifty. Process a sequence of actions. A bathe action reduces cleanliness by twenty and removes two from water volume. A shock action reduces chemical reserve by ten and increases cleanliness to one hundred. A filter action increases cleanliness by ten without using chemicals. Cleanliness cannot exceed one hundred. If chemical reserve is too low for a shock, the action is ignored. Return the final cleanliness, chemical reserve, and water volume. Example input: ["bathe", "bathe", "shock", "filter"]. Output: (100, 40, 496).

title: Forklift Hydraulic Lift
spec: The entry function is `operate(commands)`. Simulate a forklift with a mast and a set of forks. The mast tracks its tilt angle starting at zero and a max weight limit of two thousand. The forks track their current height starting at zero and current load weight starting at zero. For a lift command with a number, increase the height by that number if it does not exceed forty. For a lower command with a number, decrease the height by that amount, not going below zero. A load command with a weight adds it to the current load only if height is zero and total weight is within the max limit. A tilt command with a number changes the tilt angle between negative five and fifteen. Return the final height, load weight, and tilt angle. Example input: ["tilt 5", "load 1000", "lift 20"]. Output: (20, 1000, 5).

title: Paper Shredder Motor
spec: The entry function is `shred(batches)`. Create a shredder with a motor and a bin. The motor tracks its temperature starting at seventy and its operational status starting at idle. The bin tracks its capacity initially zero and a maximum of one hundred. Process a list of page counts. For each count, if the motor temperature exceeds one hundred twenty or the bin capacity plus count exceeds one hundred, change status to error and stop processing. Otherwise, set status to running, add the count to the bin, and increase motor temperature by the count divided by two. After every batch, simulate a cooldown by dropping temperature by five, but not below seventy. Return the final motor status, temperature, and bin capacity. Example input: [20, 40]. Output: ("running", 90, 60).

title: Rainwater Harvesting Tank
spec: The entry function is `collect(weather)`. Model a harvesting system comprising a collection roof and a storage tank. The roof tracks its debris level initially zero. The tank tracks its water volume initially zero and an overflow count initially zero. Process a list of weather events. A dry event increases debris level by one. A rain event with an amount washes all debris away; if debris was above three, the water is discarded. Otherwise, the amount multiplied by ten is added to the tank. If tank volume exceeds one thousand, cap it at one thousand and increment the overflow count by one. Return the final water volume, debris level, and overflow count. Example input: ["dry", "dry", "rain 5", "dry", "rain 10"]. Output: (150, 0, 0).

title: Skateboard Vert Ramp
spec: The entry function is `score(tricks)`. Manage a skateboard run and a judging panel. The run tracks consecutive landed tricks initially zero and a base score initially zero. The panel tracks the highest single trick score initially zero. Process a list of trick definitions, each being a base value and a landed boolean. If the trick is landed, increase the consecutive count by one, calculate the trick score as base value plus five for each consecutive trick prior to this one, add to base score, and update the highest trick score if applicable. If not landed, reset consecutive count to zero and add zero to base score. Return the total score, highest single trick score, and final consecutive count. Example input: [[10, True], [20, True], [15, False]]. Output: (35, 25, 0).

title: Olive Oil Press
spec: The entry function is `press(batches)`. Simulate an olive press with a grinding stone and a decanter. The stone tracks its speed initially zero and total run time initially zero. The decanter tracks collected oil ounces initially zero and is full initially false. Process a list of batch weights. For each weight, if it is less than five, ignore it. Otherwise, increase stone speed to five hundred, add the weight to total run time, and extract oil equal to weight times two. Add the extracted oil to collected ounces. After processing all batches, if collected ounces exceed one hundred, set full to true. Return the final stone speed, total run time, collected oil, and full status. Example input: [10, 3, 20]. Output: (500, 30, 60, False).

title: Soap Extrusion Press
spec: The entry function is `extrude(commands)`. Model a soap press with a hopper and an extrusion die. The hopper holds raw soap initially fifty units. The die tracks current shape initially round and heat level initially low. Process commands. A shape command followed by a word changes the die shape. A heat command followed by a word changes the heat level. A press command followed by a number attempts to extrude that many soap bars. Each bar requires two units of raw soap. If the hopper lacks enough soap, extrude as many as possible. If heat level is low, each pressed bar takes three units of soap instead. Return the final hopper amount, total bars extruded, and final die shape. Example input: ["heat high", "shape square", "press 10"]. Output: (30, 10, "square").

title: Bungee Jump Cord Tracker
spec: The entry function is `jump(weights)`. Track a bungee cord and a jump log. The cord has a base elasticity initially one hundred, a wear counter initially zero, and a maximum weight limit of three hundred. The log stores total successful jumps initially zero. Iterate over a list of jumper weights. If a weight exceeds the max limit, the jump is rejected. Otherwise, process the jump: increase total jumps by one, increase wear by the weight divided by fifty, and reduce elasticity by one for every five points of wear. If elasticity drops below fifty, the cord is retired and no more jumps are processed. Return the total successful jumps, final elasticity, and final wear counter. Example input: [150, 200]. Output: (2, 99, 7).

title: Paint Drying Booth
spec: The entry function is `dry(items)`. Create a booth with a heater and an exhaust fan. The heater tracks its temperature initially seventy. The exhaust fan tracks its speed initially zero. Process a list of items where each is a paint type and thickness. For enamel, set heater to one hundred and fan to fifty. For acrylic, set heater to eighty and fan to twenty. For each unit of thickness above ten, add two to the heater temperature and one to the fan speed. Calculate the drying time as temperature plus fan speed divided by two. Sum the drying times for all items. Return the total drying time, final heater temperature, and final fan speed. Example input: [["enamel", 12], ["acrylic", 5]]. Output: (128, 80, 20).

title: Food Truck Griddle
spec: The entry function is `cook(orders)`. Manage a food truck with a flat top griddle and a tip jar. The griddle tracks its temperature initially three hundred and clean status initially true. The tip jar holds money initially zero. For each order, which consists of a burger count and a complexity rating, increase griddle temperature by the burger count multiplied by five. If temperature exceeds three hundred fifty, two burgers burn and are discarded from the order. Serve the remaining burgers, adding five to the tip jar for each. If complexity rating is above five, set clean status to false. Return the final tip jar money, griddle temperature, and clean status. Example input: [[3, 4], [10, 6]]. Output: (55, 365, False).

title: Cotton Candy Spinner
spec: The entry function is `spin(adjustments)`. Create a cotton candy system with a spinner head and a heat element. The head tracks its speed initially zero and total sugar processed initially zero. The heat element tracks its temperature initially zero. Process a list of tuples containing speed change, heat change, and duration. For each adjustment, add the speed change to the current speed, ensuring it remains between zero and fifteen. Add the heat change to the temperature, bounded between zero and twelve. Add to the total sugar processed the product of the current speed and duration. Return the final speed, final temperature, and total sugar. Example input: [[5, 2, 10], [-2, -1, 5]]. Output: (3, 1, 65).

title: Sailplane Tow Release
spec: The entry function is `tow(phases)`. Model a glider towing mechanism comprising a tow hook and a tension sensor. The hook is initially closed. The tension sensor tracks peak tension initially zero and current tension initially zero. Process a list of phase tension changes. For each change, add it to the current tension. If current tension goes below zero, set it to zero. If current tension exceeds peak tension, update peak tension. If current tension ever exceeds five hundred, the tow hook automatically opens for safety. If a phase change is exactly nine hundred ninety nine, manually open the hook. Once the hook is open, subsequent phases are ignored and current tension drops to zero. Return the hook status as boolean where true is open, peak tension, and final current tension. Example input: [100, 50, 400, 50]. Output: (True, 550, 0).

title: Billiards Coin Mechanism
spec: The entry function is `unlock(coins)`. Manage a pool table coin chute and a ball release trapdoor. The coin chute tracks collected quarters initially zero and requires four quarters to unlock. The trapdoor tracks its state initially closed and total game count initially zero. Process a list of inserted coin values. For each quarter value of twenty five, add one to the collected quarters. If a dime or nickel is inserted, it is rejected and ignored. When collected quarters reaches four, the trapdoor state becomes open, total game count increases by one, and collected quarters resets to zero. If a pull action is in the list, it closes the trapdoor if it was open. Return the total game count, collected quarters, and trapdoor state. Example input: [25, 10, 25, 25, 25, "pull", 25]. Output: (1, 1, "closed").

title: Rain Gutter Cleaner
spec: The entry function is `clean(sections)`. Simulate a gutter sweeping robot with a drive track and a cleaning brush. The drive track tracks total distance initially zero and battery level initially one hundred. The brush tracks dirt collected initially zero and is currently active. For each section length and dirt amount, if battery level is above zero, move the track by the section length, decreasing battery by the length divided by two. If the track moves, the brush collects the dirt, adding it to dirt collected and decreasing battery by dirt amount divided by five. If battery drops to or below zero, set active to false and stop. Return total distance, dirt collected, and battery level. Example input: [[10, 20], [20, 10]]. Output: (30, 30, 81).

title: Violin String Tuner
spec: The entry function is `tune(actions)`. Model a violin pegbox and a single string. The pegbox tracks gear wear initially zero and a slip threshold initially fifty. The string tracks current pitch initially four hundred and tension initially ten. Process a sequence of actions. A tighten action increases tension by two and pitch by five. A loosen action decreases tension by one and pitch by three. A play action increases gear wear by one. If gear wear exceeds the slip threshold, any subsequent tighten action instead reduces pitch by ten and tension by five due to slipping. Return the final pitch, tension, and gear wear. Example input: ["tighten", "play", "tighten"]. Output: (410, 14, 1).

title: Cheese Vat Coagulator
spec: The entry function is `coagulate(steps)`. Create a cheese vat and an agitator. The vat tracks milk volume initially five hundred, rennet added initially false, and curd firmness initially zero. The agitator tracks its speed initially zero. Process steps. A stir step with a speed sets the agitator speed. A rennet step sets rennet added to true. A wait step with a time increases curd firmness by the time multiplied by two, but only if rennet is added and agitator speed is zero. If agitator speed is greater than zero while waiting with rennet, firmness decreases by the time. Return final curd firmness, agitator speed, and rennet status. Example input: ["rennet", "stir 0", "wait 10", "stir 5"]. Output: (20, 5, True).

title: Player Piano Tracker
spec: The entry function is `play(perforations)`. Simulate a player piano with a foot pump bellows and a pneumatic reading bar. The bellows track air pressure initially fifty. The reading bar tracks notes struck initially zero and total paper scrolled initially zero. Process a sequence of paper advancement steps. A step is an integer representing the number of holes. For each step, if air pressure is greater than the number of holes, subtract the holes from air pressure, increase notes struck by the holes, and add one to paper scrolled. If air pressure is insufficient, a pump action automatically occurs, adding forty to air pressure without scrolling the paper, and then the step is retried. A zero hole step adds twenty to air pressure. Return notes struck, paper scrolled, and air pressure. Example input: [2, 5, 0, 4]. Output: (11, 3, 59).

title: Rock Crusher Mechanism
spec: The entry function is `crush(rocks)`. Manage a jaw crusher and a conveyor belt. The jaw crusher tracks its wear level initially zero and current gap size initially five. The conveyor tracks tons processed initially zero. Process a list of rock sizes. If a rock size is larger than the gap size plus ten, it jams; increase wear level by five and ignore the rock. Otherwise, the rock is crushed, adding its size to tons processed, and increasing wear level by one. If wear level exceeds fifty, the gap size increases to eight. Return tons processed, wear level, and gap size. Example input: [12, 20, 8]. Output: (20, 6, 5).

title: Parachute Deployment Altimeter
spec: The entry function is `fall(readings)`. Build a skydiving altimeter containing a barometer and a deployment switch. The barometer tracks current altitude initially ten thousand and descent rate initially zero. The switch tracks deployment status initially false and reserve deployed initially false. Process a list of altitude readings. For each reading, calculate descent rate as previous altitude minus current altitude, then update current altitude. If descent rate exceeds one hundred and current altitude is below three thousand, set deployment status to true. If current altitude falls below one thousand and descent rate still exceeds fifty, set reserve deployed to true. Return deployment status, reserve deployed, and final descent rate. Example input: [9000, 5000, 2000]. Output: (True, False, 3000).

title: Telegraph Relay Station
spec: Write a simulation of a telegraph relay station tracking incoming electrical pulses. The station manages multiple lines, each maintaining its own buffer of dots and dashes, current word, and list of completed words. A pulse can be short, long, or a pause. Short pulses add a dot, long pulses add a dash, and pauses resolve the current buffer into a letter and append it to the current word. A long pause resolves the word. The main system routes pulses to the correct line based on an integer identifier. Return a list of completed sentences for each line. Example: sending a sequence of shorts and longs to line one produces the letter a. Entry function: `relay(pulses)`

title: Mechanical Metronome
spec: Model a mechanical metronome with a spring tension and a sliding pendulum weight. The metronome holds a current tempo in beats per minute, determined by the weight position, and a stored spring energy level. Winding adds a specific amount of energy to the spring. Moving the weight up decreases the tempo, while moving it down increases the tempo. Ticking consumes energy proportional to the tempo and produces a tick sound. If energy is depleted, the metronome stops. The system should process a sequence of actions like wind, move weight, and tick, returning a count of successful ticks. Example: winding ten units and ticking at a high tempo might produce fewer ticks than at a low tempo. Entry function: `tick(actions)`

title: Antikythera Gear Calculator
spec: Simulate an ancient geared calculator predicting astronomical positions. The main drive wheel tracks its rotational angle and connects to several smaller gear trains representing the sun, the moon, and the eclipse cycle. Turning the main drive by a specified number of teeth causes the connected gears to rotate according to their specific gear ratios. The moon gear train includes a mechanical pin and slot that slightly accelerates and decelerates its motion to simulate an elliptical orbit. Process a sequence of turns applied to the main drive and return the final angular positions of all celestial indicators. Example: advancing the drive by one full year completes one solar rotation but multiple lunar rotations. Entry function: `antikythera(turns)`

title: Analog Synthesizer Oscillator
spec: Simulate an analog synthesizer with independent voltage controlled oscillators and a mixer. Each oscillator maintains a frequency, a waveform shape like square or triangle, and a current phase angle. Advancing time steps updates the phase angle of each oscillator based on its frequency and calculates the current voltage output. The mixer combines the voltages from all active oscillators, applying a volume multiplier. Process a list of control signals to change frequencies or mute oscillators over time, and output a list of final mixed voltage values for each time step. Example: mixing two oscillators at slightly different frequencies produces a beating wave output. Entry function: `synthesize(signals)`

title: Pneumatic Tube Dispatch
spec: Design a pneumatic tube message system with a central pressure pump and several destination stations. The pump maintains a vacuum pressure that regenerates over time but drops sharply when a capsule is sent. Each station holds a queue of outgoing capsules waiting for sufficient pressure. During each time step, the system regenerates a fixed amount of pressure. If a station has a waiting capsule and the pump pressure is above the required threshold, the capsule is dispatched, reducing the pressure. Process a timeline of capsules arriving at stations and return a list of dispatch times for each capsule. Example: a high arrival rate causes delays due to low pressure. Entry function: `dispatch(events)`

title: Mechanical Music Box
spec: Simulate a mechanical music box containing a rotating pinned cylinder and a tuned metal comb. The comb consists of multiple teeth, each representing a different musical note and having a specific fatigue level. The cylinder stores a sequence of pins that pluck specific teeth at specific rotational angles. Advancing the mechanism rotates the cylinder one step, plucking the corresponding teeth. Plucking a tooth increases its fatigue, and if fatigue exceeds a threshold, the tooth breaks and no longer sounds. Given a layout of pins and a number of rotations, return the sequence of notes that successfully sound. Example: playing the same note repeatedly may cause it to break. Entry function: `play(rotations)`

title: Diving Bell Compressor
spec: Model a diving bell system with a surface air compressor and an underwater bell chamber. The compressor tracks its motor temperature and pumping rate. The bell tracks its depth, internal air pressure, and breathable oxygen ratio. Lowering the bell increases external water pressure, requiring the compressor to pump more air to equalize. Pumping air restores oxygen but raises the compressor temperature. If the compressor overheats, it must rest, causing oxygen in the bell to slowly deplete. Process a sequence of depth changes and rest periods, returning a list of oxygen levels at each step. Example: descending too fast overworks the compressor and reduces air quality. Entry function: `dive(events)`

title: Hot Metal Typesetter
spec: Create a simulation of a mechanical typesetting machine that manages a magazine of letter matrices and a crucible of molten lead. The magazine tracks the count of available brass molds for each letter of the alphabet. Pressing a key drops a mold into the assembly line. When a line is complete, the casting mechanism pours lead from the crucible to form a solid text slug, consuming lead mass, and then the molds are returned to the magazine. If a letter is out of stock or lead is depleted, the line fails. Given a sequence of words to type, return the successfully cast lines. Example: typing the same letter too many times without casting exhausts the magazine. Entry function: `typeset(words)`

title: Theater Stage Rigging
spec: Manage a theater stage rigging system with multiple lifting lines and a counterweight arbor. Each lifting line connects to a scenery piece with a specific weight and tracks its height above the stage. The arbor holds iron weights that can be added or removed. To move a scenery piece, the arbor weight must exactly match the scenery weight, otherwise the movement fails due to imbalance. Process a sequence of stage cues that specify adding weights, removing weights, and pulling specific lines up or down. Return the final heights of all scenery pieces. Example: lifting a heavy backdrop requires loading the arbor first. Entry function: `rigging(cues)`

title: Vintage Jukebox Selector
spec: Simulate a classic jukebox mechanism comprising a coin accumulator and a rotating record carousel. The accumulator tracks inserted coins and converts them into song credits based on pricing tiers. The carousel holds records in numbered slots and tracks its current rotational position. When a song is selected, the system checks for available credits. If a credit is available, it is consumed, the carousel rotates to the shortest path to the target slot, and the record plays. Process a series of coin insertions and song selections, returning the total rotational distance the carousel traveled. Example: selecting a sequence of adjacent slots minimizes travel distance. Entry function: `jukebox(actions)`

title: Papermaking Pulp Vat
spec: Model a hand papermaking process with a pulp vat and a molding frame. The vat tracks total water volume and grams of cellulose fiber. The frame tracks the accumulated fiber thickness. Adding raw materials increases the vat contents. Dipping the frame extracts a specific volume of the mixture, removing both water and fiber from the vat, and deposits the fiber onto the frame to form a sheet. The thickness of the sheet depends on the fiber concentration in the vat at the moment of the dip. Given a sequence of adding materials and dipping, return a list of sheet thicknesses produced. Example: repeated dipping without replenishing yields progressively thinner sheets. Entry function: `papermill(steps)`

title: Mechanical Sorting Centrifuge
spec: Design a simulation of an industrial centrifuge used to separate mixed materials. The system includes a motor tracking revolutions per minute and a spinning drum holding particles with different mass values. Engaging the motor increases the speed incrementally. As speed increases, particles are ejected from the drum based on their mass thresholds, with heavier particles ejecting at lower speeds. Applying the brake reduces speed. Process a list of commands to load particles, accelerate, and decelerate, and return a list indicating the speed at which each particle was ejected. Example: a slow acceleration safely separates heavy elements first. Entry function: `centrifuge(commands)`

title: Glassblowing Annealing Lehr
spec: Simulate a glass annealing lehr oven that slowly cools blown glass to prevent shattering. The lehr consists of several sequential temperature zones and a moving conveyor belt. Each glass piece tracks its current temperature, structural stress level, and position on the belt. As the belt advances, pieces move between zones and their temperature approaches the zone temperature. Rapid temperature drops increase structural stress. If stress exceeds a critical limit, the piece shatters and is removed. Process a list of initial glass pieces passing through defined zone temperatures and return the count of surviving pieces. Example: a steep temperature gradient causes all pieces to shatter. Entry function: `anneal(batches)`

title: Sundial Shadow Calculator
spec: Create a simulation of a sundial gnomon casting shadows based on solar positioning. The sundial maintains its geographic latitude and the height of its central pointer. The sun tracker component calculates the solar elevation and azimuth angles given a day of the year and an hour of the day. The sundial uses these angles to compute the length and compass direction of the resulting shadow. If the sun is below the horizon, no shadow is cast. For a given list of days and hours, return a sequence of calculated shadow lengths. Example: noon in summer produces the shortest shadow length. Entry function: `sundial(times)`

title: Mechanical Combination Safe
spec: Model a rotary combination lock mechanism with three internal wheel tumblers and a central spindle. The spindle tracks its current rotational angle. Turning the dial engages the first tumbler, which then catches the second, and finally the third, updating their respective angles based on rotation direction and distance. The lock opens only if the three tumblers match a secret sequence of angles. Process a list of turning actions specifying direction and degrees, and then an attempt to pull the handle. Return true if the safe opens, false otherwise. Example: alternating directions correctly aligns the tumblers to open the lock. Entry function: `unlock(turns)`

title: Trebuchet Counterweight
spec: Simulate a medieval trebuchet tracking a hinged throwing arm, a counterweight box, and a sling holding a projectile. The counterweight box tracks its loaded mass. The arm tracks its pivot ratio. When released, the potential energy of the falling counterweight transfers to the sling, calculating a launch velocity based on the projectile mass and the arm ratio. Loading stones increases the counterweight mass. Firing launches the projectile and records its travel distance. Process a sequence of loading counterweights, loading projectiles, and firing, returning the distances achieved. Example: a massive counterweight with a light projectile yields a massive distance. Entry function: `siege(commands)`

title: Candle Dipping Carousel
spec: Manage a traditional candle making carousel that rotates multiple hanging wicks over a vat of hot wax. The carousel tracks its current rotational position and an array of wicks, each with a current wax thickness and core temperature. The vat maintains its liquid wax level. Rotating the carousel advances the position. Dipping submerges the current wick, consuming wax from the vat and increasing the wick thickness, provided the wick has cooled sufficiently since its last dip. If dipped while too hot, the wax melts off instead. Process a sequence of rotations, delays, and dips, returning the final thickness of each candle. Example: spacing dips with delays builds thickness properly. Entry function: `candle(operations)`

title: Steamboat Paddlewheel
spec: Simulate a river steamboat managing a wood fired boiler and a massive paddlewheel. The boiler tracks its internal steam pressure and wood inventory. Adding wood and stoking the fire increases steam pressure. The paddlewheel uses steam pressure to rotate, consuming the steam and generating forward thrust. The river provides a constant opposing current drag. The boat tracks its overall distance traveled along the river. Process a timeline of stoking the fire, releasing steam to the wheel, and coasting, returning the total distance traveled. Example: releasing steam without sufficient pressure results in the river pushing the boat backwards. Entry function: `navigate(intervals)`

title: Water Clock Clepsydra
spec: Model an ancient water clock consisting of an upper reservoir, a drip valve, and a lower measuring basin. The upper reservoir tracks its water volume, which affects the internal water pressure. The drip valve has an adjustable opening size. Water drips into the lower basin at a rate determined by both the valve size and the upper reservoir pressure. The lower basin contains a float that rises with the water level, tracking the elapsed time. Process a sequence of valve adjustments and time intervals, returning the final estimated time reading from the lower basin. Example: as the upper reservoir empties, the drip rate slows down, causing the clock to lose time. Entry function: `clepsydra(events)`

title: Astrolabe Navigator
spec: Model an antique astrolabe instrument used for celestial navigation. The instrument consists of a stationary base plate calibrated for a specific latitude and a rotating celestial sphere net. The net tracks the angular positions of several bright stars. Rotating the net aligns a selected star with an observed altitude angle on the base plate, allowing the user to read off the estimated local solar time. Process a sequence of star sightings, rotating the net to match the observed altitude for each, and return the calculated local time for each observation. Example: observing the dog star at its peak altitude yields midnight. Entry function: `astrolabe(sightings)`

title: Clockwork Automaton
spec: Simulate an antique clockwork automaton figure driven by a mainspring and a cylinder of mechanical cams. The mainspring tracks its wound tension level. The cylinder features multiple tracks of cams, each triggering a different limb movement. Winding the spring increases tension. Releasing the brake allows the cylinder to rotate, consuming tension for each degree of rotation and triggering limb movements when a cam is encountered. Process a sequence of winding operations and running intervals, returning a list of the sequential movements performed. Example: a fully wound spring plays out the entire cylinder sequence of arm waves and head nods. Entry function: `animate(winds)`

title: Hand Crank Phonograph
spec: Design a simulation of an early cylinder phonograph featuring a hand crank, a tension spring, and an acoustic sound box. The spring stores rotational energy. The crank adds energy to the spring up to a maximum limit. The sound box tracks its position along a wax cylinder containing audio grooves. Releasing the spring rotates the cylinder, consuming energy and advancing the sound box position to read out audio samples. If the spring depletes, playback stops prematurely. Process a sequence of cranking amounts and playback durations, returning the extracted audio samples. Example: insufficient cranking cuts the song off halfway. Entry function: `phonograph(actions)`

title: Grain Mill Waterwheel
spec: Model a traditional watermill managing a sluice gate, a waterwheel, and two grinding stones. The sluice gate controls the volume of water hitting the wheel, tracking its open percentage. The waterwheel converts water volume into rotational speed. The grinding stones process raw grain from a hopper into flour at a rate directly proportional to the rotational speed, wearing down the stones over time. Worn stones produce less flour per rotation. Process a sequence of sluice gate adjustments and grain dumps, returning the total pounds of flour produced. Example: opening the gate fully grinds grain rapidly but accelerates stone wear. Entry function: `mill(flows)`

title: Telegraph Tape Puncher
spec: Simulate a mechanical paper tape punch machine used for telegraphy. The machine tracks a continuous strip of paper, the current lengthwise position, and a set of five piercing pins. For each letter typed on the keyboard, a specific combination of pins activates to punch holes across the width of the tape, and the paper advances one step. The machine tracks the total length of paper consumed and the pattern of holes at each position. Given a string of letters, look up the pin combinations and return the sequence of punched hole arrays along with the total paper length used. Example: typing a short word punches a sequence of distinct five bit binary patterns. Entry function: `punch(messages)`

title: Photographic Enlarger
spec: Create a simulation of a darkroom photographic enlarger tracking a halogen bulb, a focus lens, and light sensitive paper. The bulb maintains a temperature and emits light intensity based on its wattage. The lens tracks an aperture setting that restricts the light passing through. Leaving the bulb on exposes the paper, increasing its darkness level, but heats up the bulb. If the bulb exceeds a safe temperature, it damages the negative. Turning the bulb off allows it to cool. Process a sequence of aperture adjustments and exposure durations, returning the final darkness level of the paper or an error if damaged. Example: long exposures require cooling intervals between them to prevent damage. Entry function: `enlarge(exposures)`

title: Shipping Network Hub
spec: Write a function `simulate(manifest)` that models a freight routing network. The logic requires creating a central dispatch entity and multiple warehouse entities. The dispatch entity tracks all registered warehouses and handles the insertion of incoming boxes based on their destination tag. Each warehouse entity maintains a list of stored boxes and a maximum capacity limit. If a warehouse is full, the dispatch entity must hold the box in a secondary overflow queue. The function takes a list of string tuples representing box identifiers and destination warehouse names. It returns a list of integer pairs showing the final count of boxes in each warehouse and the count in the overflow queue.

title: Software Bug Tracker
spec: Develop a function `triage(issues)` that processes a list of software defects. Implement a main project tracking entity that manages individual defect entities and programmer entities. Each defect entity tracks its urgency level, a brief description, and its resolution status. Each programmer entity keeps a list of currently assigned defects and a maximum workload limit. The tracking entity iterates through incoming defects and assigns them to the programmer with the lowest current workload, provided they have not reached their limit. The function takes a list of string tuples describing incoming defects and their urgency, and returns a list of programmer names with their total assigned defect counts.

title: Real Estate Agency
spec: Create a function `evaluate(listings)` that manages a housing market simulation. The architecture must include an agency entity, broker entities, and property entities. Property entities store their base price, neighborhood zone, and sale status. Broker entities maintain a sales quota and a list of active properties they represent. The agency entity receives a sequence of property listings, creates the property entities, and assigns them in an alternating round robin fashion to three available brokers. If a property is marked as a luxury zone, its base price gets an automatic percentage increase before assignment. The function processes a list of price and zone tuples, applies the assignments, and returns the total projected revenue for each broker.

title: Zoo Habitat Organizer
spec: Design a function `allocate(animals)` to distribute incoming creatures into appropriate wildlife sanctuaries. The system relies on a main park entity that holds several enclosure entities. Each enclosure entity is strictly defined by a climate type, a current resident count, and a strict capacity limit. The park entity receives requests to house new creatures, verifies their required climate, and places them into the first enclosure that matches the climate and has available space. If no space exists across any matching enclosures, the creature is rejected. The function accepts a list of creature names and their preferred climates, and returns the final number of residents in each enclosure along with a count of rejected creatures.

title: Galactic Mining Fleet
spec: Implement a function `mine(targets)` that simulates a deep space resource extraction operation. You must build a command entity that controls multiple extractor vessel entities. Each vessel entity tracks its cargo hold capacity, current mineral load, and fuel reserves. The command entity reviews a list of asteroid coordinates and dispatches the vessel with the highest current fuel reserves to extract minerals. Extracting minerals increases the vessel load and decreases its fuel by fixed amounts. Once a vessel is full, it cannot be dispatched until the command entity unloads it. The function takes a list of integers representing extraction yields and returns a sequence of the final cargo loads of all vessels.

title: Judicial Court Docket
spec: Write a function `schedule(cases)` that assigns legal disputes to available magistrates. The logic requires a central courthouse entity that oversees magistrate entities and dispute entities. Each magistrate entity has a specific expertise area and a maximum daily hours limit. Dispute entities track their required time block and subject matter. The courthouse attempts to match each incoming dispute to a magistrate who shares the required expertise and has enough remaining daily hours to handle the time block. If a match is found, the magistrate hours are reduced accordingly.
